summary: Data augmentation improves visual recognition by exposing models to synthetic training examples that encourage generalization beyond the observed data. Mixed-sample methods extend this idea by combining multiple images. However, many common approaches either mix only pairs of images or rely on fixed small layouts, limiting control over source count, visible area proportions, and induced supervision. We propose TreemapMix, a distribution-controlled multi-image augmentation that samples source weights from a Dirichlet distribution and assigns them to area-proportional regions using a treemap partition. The resulting known region areas support two complementary objectives. TreemapMix with soft cross-entropy (SCE) treats areas as soft class-probability targets, while TreemapMix with a Plackett-Luce (PL) objective converts areas into ordinal supervision. On ImageNet-1K under matched training recipes, TreemapMix-SCE achieves substantially lower calibration error than evaluated mixed-sample baselines, while TreemapMix-PL achieves the strongest Top-1 accuracy. Transfer experiments on object detection and instance segmentation suggest that TreemapMix-pretrained features remain useful beyond classification. These results show that controlled multi-image composition can expose the same region-area information as either probability-matching or rank-matching supervision. Code is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: TreemapMix is a multi-image augmentation that samples source weights from a Dirichlet distribution and places images into area-proportional treemap regions. On ImageNet-1K, the soft cross-entropy variant gives the lowest calibration error and the Plackett-Luce variant gives the best Top-1 accuracy.
AI.motivation: Common mixed-sample methods mix only pairs of images or rely on fixed small layouts, which limits control over source count, visible area proportions and induced supervision.
AI.method: Dirichlet-sampled source weights are assigned to treemap partitions, so that region areas serve either as soft class-probability targets (TreemapMix with SCE) or as ordinal supervision through a Plackett-Luce objective (TreemapMix-PL).
AI.result: Under matched training recipes on ImageNet-1K, TreemapMix-SCE achieves substantially lower calibration error than the evaluated mixed-sample baselines, and TreemapMix-PL achieves the strongest Top-1 accuracy. Transfer experiments on object detection and instance segmentation suggest the pretrained features remain useful.
AI.conclusion: Controlled multi-image composition can expose the same region-area information as either probability-matching or rank-matching supervision.

title: BudSplat: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting under a Rendering Budget
summary: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting has recently emerged as a promising alternative to per-scene optimization, enabling fast novel view synthesis by predicting Gaussian primitives directly from input images. However, it quickly faces a bottleneck of rendering efficiency while scaling from sparse to dense multi-view inputs, which offer more geometric constraints but produce a rapidly growing set of candidate Gaussians. Existing solutions cannot reliably distinguish redundant primitives, leading to many redundant primitives from repeatedly observed regions and increased rendering cost without much gain in visual quality. We propose BudSplat, a compact feed-forward 3DGS framework that learns to keep the most valuable Gaussians under a limited primitive count. BudSplat has two novel designs. The first is a detail-aware importance score that is extracted from multi-level visual tokens, providing an explicit cue for regions where pruning is likely to harm perceptual quality. The score can be injected into voxel fusion to preserve high-value local contributors during multi-view aggregation. The second is quality-aware Gaussian pruning that selects a compact set of primitives by jointly considering rendering contribution and detail importance. The quality-aware pruning enables local quota redistribution that helps avoid over-allocating primitives to large redundant regions. Experiments on RE10K, DL3DV, and ACID show that BudSplat achieves a favorable trade-off among rendering quality and efficiency.

AI.tldr: BudSplat is a feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that keeps the most valuable Gaussians under a limited primitive count. It achieves a favourable trade-off between rendering quality and efficiency on RE10K, DL3DV and ACID.
AI.motivation: Scaling feed-forward 3DGS from sparse to dense multi-view inputs produces a rapidly growing set of candidate Gaussians, many redundant, which raises rendering cost without much gain in visual quality, and existing methods cannot reliably distinguish redundant primitives.
AI.method: A detail-aware importance score extracted from multi-level visual tokens is injected into voxel fusion to preserve high-value local contributors. Quality-aware Gaussian pruning jointly considers rendering contribution and detail importance and allows local quota redistribution.
AI.result: The abstract reports a favourable trade-off among rendering quality and efficiency on RE10K, DL3DV and ACID, and gives no specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Budgeted, detail-aware pruning keeps compact feed-forward reconstructions from over-allocating primitives to large redundant regions.

title: ConvRoute-ViT: Convolutional Token Routing for Efficient Vision Transformers
summary: Vision Transformers (ViTs) achieve strong image recognition performance, but their self-attention increases quadratically with the number of input tokens and makes them computationally expensive. The standard implementation of ViT models treats all patch tokens with equal importance across every layer of the model. This uniform treatment introduces redundant computation and may reduce the model's focus on the most discriminative object regions. In this paper, we propose ConvRoute-ViT, a convolutional token routing mechanism for efficient vision transformers that performs token reduction through convolutional routing. Our model preserves the most relevant patch tokens according to class-token attention at selected layers, while the remaining tokens are spatially reorganized and compressed into a compact set of convolutional summary tokens. This design reduces the sequence length without completely removing the contextual information of the less informative tokens. By applying the routing process hierarchically, the proposed framework constructs compact and discriminative representations for deeper layers. Experiments on CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet show that ConvRoute-ViT improves computational efficiency while maintaining classification accuracy compared with the base ViT.

AI.tldr: ConvRoute-ViT reduces the cost of Vision Transformers by routing the most class-relevant patch tokens through and compressing the rest into convolutional summary tokens. It maintains classification accuracy compared with the base ViT on CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet while improving computational efficiency.
AI.motivation: Standard ViTs treat all patch tokens with equal importance in every layer, which introduces redundant computation and may reduce focus on the most discriminative object regions, while self-attention cost grows quadratically with token count.
AI.method: At selected layers, tokens are preserved according to class-token attention, and the remaining tokens are spatially reorganized and compressed into a compact set of convolutional summary tokens. The routing is applied hierarchically to build representations for deeper layers.
AI.result: On CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet, ConvRoute-ViT improves computational efficiency while maintaining classification accuracy compared with the base ViT; the abstract gives no specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Convolutional token routing shortens the sequence without completely discarding the context carried by less informative tokens.

title: PulmoWorld: An Asynchronous Multimodal Medical World Model for Longitudinal Pneumonia Dynamics
summary: Pneumonia changes across respiration, inflammation, and organ function, while the measurements that describe it arrive at different times and are often incomplete. We introduce PULMOWORLD, a world model for longitudinal pneumonia dynamics that connects asynchronous state estimation, recursive simulation, and evidence-constrained planning. History-aware filtering separates state propagation from observation-driven correction, so a measurement updates the shared belief only when it is observed. That belief supports recursive forecasts of clinical values and modality representations, and summaries of future prognosis. Cap-MBRL searches imagined continuations inside an authorized action set and replaces a frozen fallback only when a candidate meets the risk budget and a predicted-cost margin. On the pneumonia cohort MASS, recursive forecasts are competitive with task-trained sequence models, and simulated future states retain prognostic information. Trained separately on public MIMIC-IV-CXR chest radiographs and clinical trajectories, this model improves prognostic discrimination over latest-value fusion in development and is competitive on long-horizon error on the locked pneumonia panel. In five known-mechanism MASS-Syn environments, Cap-MBRL lowers selection regret relative to direct fallback execution.

AI.tldr: PulmoWorld is a world model for longitudinal pneumonia dynamics that handles asynchronous, often incomplete measurements and plans with Cap-MBRL under an authorized action set and risk budget. On the MASS cohort its recursive forecasts are competitive with task-trained sequence models.
AI.motivation: Pneumonia measurements arrive at different times and are often incomplete, so a model needs to update a shared belief only when an observation is actually made, and then forecast future states and prognosis.
AI.method: History-aware filtering separates state propagation from observation-driven correction. Recursive forecasts cover clinical values, modality representations and prognosis summaries, and Cap-MBRL searches imagined continuations, replacing a frozen fallback only when a candidate meets the risk budget and a predicted-cost margin.
AI.result: On MASS, recursive forecasts are competitive with task-trained sequence models and simulated future states retain prognostic information. Trained on public MIMIC-IV-CXR chest radiographs and clinical trajectories, the model improves prognostic discrimination over latest-value fusion in development and is competitive on long-horizon error on a locked panel; in five MASS-Syn environments Cap-MBRL lowers selection regret relative to direct fallback execution.
AI.conclusion: The results suggest that asynchronous world models with risk-constrained planning can support longitudinal pneumonia management.

title: Hidden Commitment: When Language Models Silently Pick a Side and How Steering Can Surface It
summary: Language-model answers are often treated as a visible record of the internal decision that produced them. We test this assumption in conflicting-context question answering, where two supplied documents support incompatible answers. A model can process the disagreement and still return a one-sided answer, even under prompts that ask it to disclose conflict. In Qwen 0.8B, hidden source commitment is captured by a residual source-choice direction whose sign tracks which document the answer uses. Sparse middle-layer MLP writers feed the same coordinate, and steering the coordinate changes the chosen source. A transfer run on Gemma 3 1B preserves the source-choice readout and sparse-write bridge under LLM-audited labels. Conflict disclosure follows a different pattern, appearing weaker, later-layer, and only partially steerable. These results support a practical monitoring strategy for retrieval systems that detects silent source commitment with residual readouts and pairs conflict-surfacing prompts with disclosure steering when the model has selected a side under disagreement.

AI.tldr: Language models can silently commit to one of two conflicting supplied documents while answering as if no conflict exists, and a residual source-choice direction reads out this commitment. Steering that direction changes the chosen source in Qwen 0.8B, and the readout transfers to Gemma 3 1B.
AI.motivation: Model answers are often treated as a faithful record of the internal decision behind them, yet a model can process a conflict and still return a one-sided answer, even when prompted to disclose the conflict.
AI.method: In conflicting-context question answering, the authors identify a residual source-choice direction whose sign tracks which document the answer uses, trace it to sparse middle-layer MLP writers, and steer the coordinate. Conflict disclosure is compared with source commitment, and the analysis is transferred to Gemma 3 1B under LLM-audited labels.
AI.result: The source-choice readout and sparse-write bridge are preserved on Gemma 3 1B, and steering the coordinate changes the chosen source. Conflict disclosure appears weaker, later-layer and only partially steerable.
AI.conclusion: Residual readouts can detect silent source commitment in retrieval systems, and pairing conflict-surfacing prompts with disclosure steering is suggested when a model has selected a side under disagreement.

title: Don't Ask the LLM: Visual Token Pruning with Spectral Structure and Semantic Relevance
comment: Accepted to WACV 2027. 19 pages (10 pages main paper, 9 pages supplementary material)
summary: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) represent images and videos as long visual-token sequences, substantially increasing inference costs. These costs motivate visual-token pruning, whose effectiveness depends on both what signal is used for selection and when that signal becomes available. Our analysis reveals complementary limitations: visual-side [CLS] attention produces scattered, background-biased selections under aggressive compression, while stronger query-conditioned signals become available after substantial computation within the large language model (LLM). This raises a natural question: can structurally coherent, query-aware token selection be performed before consulting the LLM? We therefore propose ST-Pruner (Spectral-Textual Pruner), a training-free framework for pre-LLM visual-token selection. It combines attention-independent spectral saliency with inverted patch-text similarity through parameter-free multiplicative fusion. Across diverse LVLMs, ST-Pruner retains over 95% of full-token performance using at most 11.1% of visual tokens and achieves a 3.2x end-to-end speedup on LLaVA-NeXT. Code is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: ST-Pruner is a training-free method that selects visual tokens before the LLM, combining attention-independent spectral saliency with inverted patch-text similarity. It retains over 95 percent of full-token performance using at most 11.1 percent of visual tokens and gives a 3.2x end-to-end speedup on LLaVA-NeXT.
AI.motivation: Visual-side [CLS] attention produces scattered, background-biased selections under aggressive compression, while query-conditioned signals only become available after substantial computation inside the LLM.
AI.method: Attention-independent spectral saliency is fused multiplicatively with inverted patch-text similarity using a parameter-free fusion, so that structurally coherent, query-aware tokens are selected before the LLM is consulted.
AI.result: Across diverse LVLMs, ST-Pruner retains over 95 percent of full-token performance using at most 11.1 percent of visual tokens, and achieves a 3.2x end-to-end speedup on LLaVA-NeXT.
AI.conclusion: Query-aware visual token selection can be performed before consulting the LLM, substantially reducing inference cost.

title: Extremely Sparse-View Computed Tomography from 2D Projections via Pose-Aware Diffusion Priors
summary: Extremely sparse-view computed tomography (xSV-CT) is critical when scanning time, motion, or radiation tolerance limits each scan to only a few projections. In many such scenarios, the same acquisition limits also constrain dataset construction, making pre-reconstructed 3D volumes from dense scans unavailable. This exposes a gap in current sparse-view approaches: Optimization-based methods, which use the sparse measurements directly but lack data-driven priors to suppress artifacts, and learning-based methods, which use strong priors but usually require densely scanned training volumes acquired outside the xSV-CT regime. We study this train-sparse / infer-sparse setting by learning a pose-aware diffusion prior from one 2D projection per training sample, then guiding diffusion sampling with measured-view fidelity, shared-volume reprojection, and projection-physics consistency for tomographic reconstruction. On two public CT datasets across 1-, 4-, and 8-view settings, the proposed method achieves the best novel-view synthesis scores and best or competitive reconstruction quality compared with baselines that use dense-volume supervision.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a pose-aware diffusion prior learned from one 2D projection per training sample, guided during sampling for extremely sparse-view CT reconstruction without dense 3D training volumes. It achieves the best novel-view synthesis scores and best or competitive reconstruction quality on two public CT datasets with 1, 4 and 8 views.
AI.motivation: Optimization-based sparse-view methods lack data-driven priors to suppress artifacts, while learning-based methods usually need densely scanned training volumes that cannot be acquired in the extremely sparse regime.
AI.method: A pose-aware diffusion prior is learned from single 2D projections and guided by measured-view fidelity, shared-volume reprojection and projection-physics consistency during tomographic reconstruction.
AI.result: On two public CT datasets across 1-, 4- and 8-view settings, the method achieves the best novel-view synthesis scores and best or competitive reconstruction quality compared with baselines that use dense-volume supervision.
AI.conclusion: Training and inferring in the sparse regime is feasible, so dense-scan volumes are not needed for diffusion-based sparse-view CT reconstruction.

title: SSQA: Sibling-Selective Quadtree Attention for Hierarchical Modeling in Perception Tasks
comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables. Published at ICRA 2026 (oral)
summary: Perception tasks for navigation in robotics, including aerial platforms such as drones and autonomous driving systems, are inherently structured. Drone-mounted cameras typically capture sky above, terrain below, and obstacles or man-made structures in between, while driving data often contains organized road layouts, lane markings, and surrounding agents. Motivated by these axis-aligned structural priors, we note that such information is typically more structured than in generic image tasks. We hypothesize that processing information in a quadtree-esque manner can not only model features effectively in a hierarchical manner, but also offers an efficient linear-time alternative to vanilla attention mechanisms, which run in quadratic time. In this paper, we propose Sibling-Selective Quadtree Attention (SSQA), which models image tokens hierarchically as a structured, full quadtree. We show analytical complexity analysis that guarantees linear-time feature modeling, in addition to empirical experiments comparing inference speeds with other popular modeling approaches, such as Mamba 2 and Quadtree Attention. Our results, benchmarked across several tasks, show that we achieve results at least as good, if not notably better, as others at a fraction of the computational costs.

AI.tldr: SSQA is a quadtree-style attention mechanism for image tokens that claims linear-time complexity while matching or exceeding Mamba 2 and Quadtree Attention across several perception tasks. The advantage is reported mainly in inference cost, at a fraction of the computational cost.
AI.motivation: Perception scenes for drones and autonomous driving are axis-aligned and structured, so hierarchical processing might model them efficiently, offering an alternative to quadratic-time vanilla attention.
AI.method: Sibling-Selective Quadtree Attention models image tokens hierarchically as a structured, full quadtree. The authors give an analytical complexity analysis and compare inference speeds with Mamba 2 and Quadtree Attention.
AI.result: Results across several benchmarked tasks are at least as good as, and in some cases notably better than, those of other approaches, at a fraction of the computational cost.
AI.conclusion: Structured quadtree modelling is presented as an efficient linear-time alternative to vanilla attention for structured perception tasks.

title: Knowledge-structured and evidence-aware semantic self-distillation for glomerular pathology foundation model
summary: Visual foundation models learn rich pathological morphology but lack explicit concept-level supervision. Vision--language pretraining can provide this supervision but requires costly image--text pairs. Here, we introduce GloSAGE, a semantic self-distillation framework that uses lesion profiles predicted by a pretrained visual teacher to construct structured pathology descriptions. Reliability-guided selection identifies image--text anchors, while Knowledge-Structured Pathology Text Synthesis and Evidence-Guided Negative-pair Construction account for partially observed lesions. Image--text alignment trains projection layers while retaining the frozen visual encoder; an intermediate Semantic Transfer Layer supplies features for downstream tasks. Developed on GloMillion and evaluated across seven glomerulus- and case-level cohorts, GloSAGE supported zero-shot lesion recognition, image--text retrieval, hard-negative discrimination and concept-intervention analyses. It outperformed its source visual model in most lesion-recognition tasks and improved lesion grading, while supporting competitive case-level disease classification, injury grading and baseline renal function estimation. Ablations supported the combined contributions of knowledge-structured text and evidence-guided negatives, and the intermediate transfer layer improved mean lesion-recognition ROC-AUC relative to the complete projection output. A frozen language model conditioned on GloSAGE features generated glomerular descriptions. These findings suggest that teacher-derived lesion profiles can provide annotation-efficient semantic supervision for extending a glomerular visual foundation model.

AI.tldr: GloSAGE is a semantic self-distillation framework that builds structured pathology text from lesion profiles predicted by a visual teacher, avoiding costly image-text pairs. It supports zero-shot lesion recognition and retrieval, and outperforms its source visual model in most lesion-recognition tasks.
AI.motivation: Visual foundation models learn rich pathological morphology but lack explicit concept-level supervision, while vision-language pretraining needs costly image-text pairs.
AI.method: Reliability-guided selection identifies image-text anchors. Knowledge-structured pathology text synthesis and evidence-guided negative-pair construction account for partially observed lesions, and alignment trains projection layers with a frozen visual encoder, with an intermediate Semantic Transfer Layer supplying features for downstream tasks.
AI.result: Developed on GloMillion and evaluated on seven glomerulus- and case-level cohorts, GloSAGE outperformed its source visual model in most lesion-recognition tasks, improved lesion grading, and supported competitive case-level disease classification, injury grading and baseline renal function estimation. The intermediate layer improved mean lesion-recognition ROC-AUC relative to the full projection output.
AI.conclusion: Teacher-derived lesion profiles can provide annotation-efficient semantic supervision for extending a glomerular visual foundation model.

title: Aligning Misaligned Benchmarks for Single-View Novel View Synthesis
summary: While single-view novel view synthesis methods have been dramatically enhanced recently, how to quantify their performance has yet to be standardized. In this work, we demonstrate that an important factor lies in how each method's own reference frame is aligned with the so-called ground-truth pose. Existing methods often rely on test-time optimization of target poses for this alignment, which inherently is ill-posed due to the complexity of the optimization landscape of camera poses vs render accuracy, leading to methods being evaluated at an arbitrary local optimum. Some recognize this limitation and thus rely on 3D reconstructions of entire scenes using training and test views to align poses, which may be infeasible. In this work, instead, we propose to use traditional 2D-to-2D and 2D-to-3D image matching techniques to align 3D reconstructions. We also evaluate only within co-visible regions, between different views, which is the only place where a `correct' ground truth can be defined. Our evaluations show that with proper coordinate alignment, novel-view synthesis methods that use explicit 3D Gaussians achieve the state of the art, despite being previously reported in the literature to be outperformed by pure image-based 2D methods. We further provide a simple baseline that directly utilizes an off-the-shelf video generator and a feed-forward geometry estimator. Our simple baseline is already comparable to state-of-the-art methods specifically trained for novel-view synthesis, without any task-specific training.

AI.tldr: The paper argues that single-view novel view synthesis benchmarks are unreliable because aligning each method's reference frame to the ground-truth pose is ill-posed, and proposes 2D-to-2D and 2D-to-3D image matching to align 3D reconstructions, evaluated only in co-visible regions. Under this protocol, explicit 3D Gaussian methods reach state of the art, and a simple video-generator baseline is comparable to dedicated methods.
AI.motivation: Quantifying single-view novel view synthesis performance is not standardized; existing methods align target poses by test-time optimization, which is ill-posed and leaves evaluation at an arbitrary local optimum, while alternatives that reconstruct whole scenes from training and test views may be infeasible.
AI.method: Each method's 3D reconstruction is aligned to the ground-truth pose using traditional 2D-to-2D and 2D-to-3D image matching, and evaluation is restricted to regions co-visible between views; a baseline combines an off-the-shelf video generator with a feed-forward geometry estimator.
AI.result: With proper coordinate alignment, methods using explicit 3D Gaussians achieve state of the art, despite earlier reports that they were outperformed by pure image-based 2D methods; the simple baseline, with no task-specific training, is comparable to state-of-the-art methods trained specifically for novel view synthesis.
AI.conclusion: Benchmark conclusions about single-view novel view synthesis depend on how reference frames are aligned, so careful coordinate alignment is needed for fair comparison of methods.

title: WeVisCut: The Whole Editing Room in One Agent From Narration to Long-Form Video
summary: Producing long-form videos from narration requires interdependent decisions that remain coherent across shots. Existing agentic editors often use multi-stage workflows driven by general models, leaving the quality-cost trade-off of compact, task-adapted policies unclear. We address this gap with WeVisCut, a long-form script-to-video system that connects tool execution with policy learning. Its agent harness maintains shared production state so that tool feedback informs subsequent decisions and repairs. Because finished videos do not expose these decisions, our four-stage data pipeline combines editing inversion with verified replay to turn recovered editing intent into executable supervision. Applied to 3,750 finished videos, this pipeline yields over 130K training examples. We use this supervision to train a single 9B policy that coordinates production and recovers from failures within the same harness. Moreover, we introduce a 100-task benchmark and five metrics assessing editing quality and delivery reliability. Under a shared tool environment, WeVisCut substantially outperforms its base model and achieves comparable performance to Claude Opus 5 while using nearly 33x fewer generated tokens per successful output minute. It also outperforms task-matched native editors on our proposed metrics.

AI.tldr: WeVisCut is a long-form script-to-video agent that couples tool execution with learned policies. A single 9B policy trained on over 130K examples derived from finished videos reaches performance comparable to Claude Opus 5 while using nearly 33x fewer generated tokens per successful output minute.
AI.motivation: Existing agentic video editors rely on multi-stage workflows built on general-purpose models, so the quality-cost trade-off of compact, task-adapted policies is unclear, and finished videos do not expose the editing decisions needed as supervision.
AI.method: An agent harness maintains shared production state so that tool feedback informs later decisions and repairs; a four-stage data pipeline combines editing inversion with verified replay to turn recovered editing intent into executable supervision, applied to 3,750 finished videos; a single 9B policy is trained on this supervision, and a 100-task benchmark with five metrics is introduced.
AI.result: Under a shared tool environment, WeVisCut substantially outperforms its base model, reaches performance comparable to Claude Opus 5 while using nearly 33x fewer generated tokens per successful output minute, and outperforms task-matched native editors on the proposed metrics.
AI.conclusion: A compact, task-adapted policy trained on supervision recovered from finished videos can coordinate long-form production and recover from failures at much lower generation cost than a general frontier model.

title: Volley3D: Unified 3D Full-Sequence Reconstruction from Monocular Broadcasts
comment: 8 pages + 10 pages of supplementary. Videos available on the project webpage: this http URL
summary: 3D reconstruction from single-view sports broadcast is a pivotal capability for automated analytics and immersive AR/VR replays, yet notoriously ill-posed due to difficult-to-calibrate moving cameras and depth ambiguity. Unlike widely studied racket sports, team sports such as volleyball feature unpredictable multi-contact sequences and high altitude jumps. These dynamics categorically invalidate the standard planar projection assumptions relied upon by existing methods. To resolve these limitations without 3D training supervision, we propose a complete, physics-grounded pipeline tailored to monocular broadcast volleyball. First, we include a correction module to the perspective drift induced by ground-plane projection by coupling temporal jump spotting with Newtonian interpolation for 3D player placement. Second, for 3D ball trajectory estimation, we design a dedicated sub-trajectory segmentation architecture alongside a collision-matching algorithm. By anchoring physical equations to reconstructed 3D hand vertices, we lift noisy ball 2D detections into a spatiotemporally coherent 3D scene. Evaluations on multi-camera benchmarks demonstrate our approach significantly reduces 3D spatial drift compared to 2D-reprojection baselines.

AI.tldr: Volley3D is a physics-grounded pipeline that reconstructs 3D player and ball trajectories from monocular volleyball broadcast video without 3D training supervision. It significantly reduces 3D spatial drift compared with 2D-reprojection baselines on multi-camera benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing 3D reconstruction methods for sports rely on planar projection assumptions that break down in team sports such as volleyball, which feature unpredictable multi-contact sequences, high jumps and moving cameras that are hard to calibrate.
AI.method: A correction module for the perspective drift caused by ground-plane projection couples temporal jump spotting with Newtonian interpolation for 3D player placement; for the ball, a sub-trajectory segmentation architecture and a collision-matching algorithm anchor physical equations to reconstructed 3D hand vertices, lifting noisy 2D ball detections into a spatiotemporally coherent 3D scene.
AI.result: On multi-camera benchmarks the approach significantly reduces 3D spatial drift compared with 2D-reprojection baselines.
AI.conclusion: Anchoring player and ball motion to physical equations yields coherent 3D scenes from single-view broadcasts, supporting automated analytics and AR/VR replays.

title: SparseTokenGS: Gaussian-based Sparse-View CBCT Reconstruction via Reusable Token Pool
comment: 10 pages, 12 figures. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging
summary: Sparse-view cone-beam computed tomography is widely used for fast, low-dose volumetric imaging and lesion localization in dentistry and image-guided interventions, but it introduces severe artifacts. Feed-forward Gaussian methods transfer the reconstruction cost to training and decode each coordinate from projection-aligned features and neighboring anchors. However, information from the whole scan is written only when the field is constructed and cannot be retrieved during coordinate decoding, leaving the volume inconsistent within the scan. This is a common limitation of such methods: once the field is fixed, decoding uses only local features and reconstruction quality drops substantially. We propose SparseTokenGS, a Gaussian-based method for sparse-view cone-beam computed tomography reconstruction via a reusable token pool. Anchor Token Fusion and Point-Token Attention query this shared pool at the anchors and at the query coordinates, respectively. The local Gaussian prior is retained, and the volume is reconstructed in one forward pass, without per-scan optimization or a projection-domain loss. On three public chest and dental datasets, SparseTokenGS achieves the highest reconstruction performance among the compared methods. On clinical dental scans, reconstruction from only six projections reaches 29.51 decibels in peak signal-to-noise ratio and a structural similarity of 0.842 against the full-view reference, and off-the-shelf tooth-and-pulp segmentation keeps these structures separable for root-canal localization. Experiments on volcanic rock and chicken show performance after same-object adaptation. A reusable token pool gives feed-forward reconstruction a mechanism that keeps scan-wide context available through decoding and can benefit future rapid clinical lesion localization and analysis. The code is available at: this https URL.

AI.tldr: SparseTokenGS is a feed-forward Gaussian method for sparse-view cone-beam CT that queries a reusable token pool holding scan-wide context during coordinate decoding. From only six projections on clinical dental scans it reaches 29.51 dB PSNR and 0.842 SSIM against the full-view reference.
AI.motivation: Feed-forward Gaussian reconstruction methods write whole-scan information only when the field is constructed, so decoding relies on local features, the volume becomes inconsistent within the scan, and reconstruction quality drops substantially.
AI.method: Anchor Token Fusion and Point-Token Attention query a shared token pool at the anchors and at the query coordinates respectively; the local Gaussian prior is kept, and the volume is reconstructed in a single forward pass without per-scan optimization or a projection-domain loss.
AI.result: On three public chest and dental datasets it achieves the highest reconstruction performance among the compared methods; on clinical dental scans, six projections give 29.51 dB PSNR and SSIM 0.842, and off-the-shelf tooth-and-pulp segmentation keeps structures separable for root-canal localization; results on volcanic rock and chicken are shown after same-object adaptation.
AI.conclusion: A reusable token pool lets feed-forward reconstruction keep scan-wide context available during decoding, which may benefit rapid clinical lesion localization and analysis.

title: Visually Irrelevant Hallucinations in Medical Vision-Language Models
summary: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) show strong performance in radiology report generation (RRG) and medical visual question answering (Med-VQA), producing free-form clinical descriptions and answers from medical images. However, they may generate clinically meaningful statements that lack visual evidence or contradict image content. We refer to these errors as visually irrelevant hallucinations and investigate them at the phrase level. We propose CLEAR (Counterfactual Localized Evaluation of Alignment and Response), a model-agnostic post-hoc framework for phrase-level hallucination risk estimation. CLEAR decomposes generated responses into visually assessable clinical phrases. For each phrase, phrase-conditioned grounding identifies a candidate visual region, which is selectively perturbed by a localized counterfactual intervention. CLEAR characterizes the intervention using two complementary auditing cues: response cues, capturing semantic and clinically meaningful changes in the generated response, and alignment cues, measuring changes in image-phrase compatibility. These cues are normalized and jointly modeled to estimate phrase-level hallucination risk. Across four datasets spanning RRG and Med-VQA, CLEAR outperforms state-of-the-art hallucination detection baselines across multiple medical and general-purpose VLMs. On MIMIC-CXR, CLEAR improves AUPRC from 85.10% to 90.23%. Its effectiveness is further validated on a GT-derived controlled VIH benchmark. These results establish visually irrelevant hallucination as an important fine-grained reliability failure mode in medical VLMs and demonstrate the value of model-agnostic visual-support auditing for more trustworthy multimodal clinical generation.

AI.tldr: The paper defines visually irrelevant hallucinations in medical VLMs and proposes CLEAR, a model-agnostic post-hoc framework that estimates phrase-level hallucination risk through localized counterfactual interventions. On MIMIC-CXR it raises AUPRC from 85.10% to 90.23%.
AI.motivation: Medical VLMs may generate clinically meaningful statements that lack visual evidence or contradict the image content in radiology report generation and medical visual question answering, and such errors need to be investigated at the phrase level.
AI.method: CLEAR decomposes responses into visually assessable clinical phrases, uses phrase-conditioned grounding to identify a candidate visual region for each, perturbs that region with a localized counterfactual intervention, and characterizes the intervention with response cues (semantic and clinically meaningful changes in the response) and alignment cues (changes in image-phrase compatibility), which are normalized and jointly modeled to estimate risk.
AI.result: Across four datasets spanning report generation and medical VQA, and across multiple medical and general-purpose VLMs, CLEAR outperforms state-of-the-art hallucination detection baselines; on MIMIC-CXR, AUPRC improves from 85.10% to 90.23%, and the method is further validated on a GT-derived controlled benchmark.
AI.conclusion: Visually irrelevant hallucination is an important fine-grained reliability failure mode in medical VLMs, and model-agnostic visual-support auditing can make multimodal clinical generation more trustworthy.

title: Structure-retained low-rank adapters for weather synthesis
summary: Real-world deployment of computer vision models, particularly in outdoor scenarios, is often limited by environmental interferences, such as adverse weather. Improving model robustness across weather conditions is thus critical for reliability. However, sourcing high-quality data relevant to isolated weather effects is a significant challenge. Most datasets include changes in dynamic elements across observations of the same scene: subjects such as pedestrians and vehicles change between shots, while camera viewpoints vary. These aspects make it difficult to decouple solely weather-induced distribution shifts from the scene. In this work, we address this with a novel weather synthesis framework that utilizes structure-retaining Low-Rank Adapters (LoRA). We analyze the attention blocks in Stable Diffusion XL (SDXL) and identify where relevant structural information is mostly processed during image-to-image translation. Through an architectural analysis of SDXL, we learn structural LoRA matrices for the corresponding blocks and then leverage them for weather synthesis, eliminating the need for external conditioning such as ControlNet. Experimental results demonstrate that our method improves upon existing synthesis approaches, achieving greater realism while preserving structure. This provides a robust pipeline for generating high-fidelity training and evaluation data for outdoor computer vision applications.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a weather synthesis framework built on structure-retaining low-rank adapters for SDXL that preserve scene structure without external conditioning such as ControlNet. The method achieves greater realism than existing synthesis approaches while preserving structure.
AI.motivation: Outdoor vision models need robustness to adverse weather, but existing datasets confound weather effects with changes in pedestrians, vehicles and camera viewpoints, which makes it hard to isolate weather-induced distribution shifts.
AI.method: The attention blocks of SDXL are analyzed to identify where structural information is mainly processed during image-to-image translation; structural LoRA matrices are learned for those blocks and used for weather synthesis in place of external conditioning.
AI.result: Experimental results show that the method improves upon existing synthesis approaches, achieving greater realism while preserving structure.
AI.conclusion: The pipeline offers a route to generating high-fidelity training and evaluation data for outdoor computer vision applications.

title: IntReal: A Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for Multimodal Interleaved Generation
summary: Humans routinely consume multimodal content, where textual and visual information is naturally interleaved. Although Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) can jointly generate text and images, multimodal interleaved generation remains largely underexplored. Progress in this area is hindered by two key limitations: (1) the lack of well-defined interleaved generation tasks and corresponding training data, and (2) the absence of fine-grained evaluation protocols that can reliably diagnose model performance across different capability dimensions. To this end, we present IntReal, comprising two complementary components: IntReal-100K, a real-world dataset of multimodal interleaved samples spanning four major categories, and the IntReal Evaluation Suite, which evaluates model performance across seven complementary dimensions using specialized expert models, enabling coarse-to-fine diagnosis. Extensive experiments validate our evaluation suite through low inter-metric redundancy (max pairwise absolute Spearman's $\rho \leq 0.42$ ), high agreement with human judgments (83.3% accuracy), and strong consistency across different expert evaluators (Spearman's $\rho > 0.9$ ), supporting the complementarity and reliability of our metrics. By benchmarking four families of UMMs, we show that IntReal Evaluation Suite reveals distinct strengths and weaknesses across models. Post-training experiments demonstrate the utility of IntReal-100K for improving interleaved generation and further show that training unimodal generation can also benefit interleaved generation. These findings suggest that interleaved generation can benefit from modality-specific optimization, rather than requiring joint text-image training at every stage.

AI.tldr: IntReal provides IntReal-100K, a real-world dataset of multimodal interleaved samples, and a seven-dimension evaluation suite for interleaved text and image generation. Benchmarking reveals distinct model strengths, and post-training on the dataset improves interleaved generation.
AI.motivation: Interleaved text-image generation in Unified Multimodal Models is underexplored, hindered by the lack of well-defined tasks and training data and by the absence of fine-grained evaluation protocols that can diagnose capabilities.
AI.method: IntReal comprises IntReal-100K, a real-world dataset spanning four major categories, and the IntReal Evaluation Suite, which scores models along seven complementary dimensions using specialized expert models for coarse-to-fine diagnosis.
AI.result: The suite shows low inter-metric redundancy (maximum pairwise absolute Spearman rho of 0.42 or less), 83.3% accuracy in agreement with human judgments, and Spearman rho above 0.9 across expert evaluators; benchmarking four families of UMMs reveals distinct strengths and weaknesses; post-training on IntReal-100K improves interleaved generation, and training on unimodal generation also benefits interleaved generation.
AI.conclusion: Interleaved generation can benefit from modality-specific optimization rather than requiring joint text-image training at every stage.

title: Automatic Iconographic Annotation of Medieval Illuminations: Comparing Generative Vision-Language Models and Supervised Discriminative Classifiers
summary: The large-scale digitisation of medieval manuscripts creates a growing need for automated iconographic indexing. We evaluate two complementary paradigms for this task on 9,735 full-folio images annotated with 2,333 TIMEL concepts: generative Vision-Language Models (VLM) and supervised discriminative classifiers (SDC). The VLM experiments evaluate fine-tuning, structured JSON decoding, taxonomybased candidates generation, and deterministic reranking. The discriminative experiments evaluate flat, hierarchy-aware, and patch-attention heads over a frozen DINOv3 encoder. Our results highlight key functional differences: ML-Decoder (SDC) achieves the strongest overall retrieval performance (precision@1 of 0.696, MRR of 0.806), with loss calibration (Asymmetric Loss) serving as the primary performance lever. While SDCs provide superior precision and reliability within a closed vocabulary, VLMs offer strong semantic generalization and broad taxonomic coverage, particularly through structured JSON targets and verify-calibrate reranking (hierarchical F1 of 0.559). Furthermore, model behavior strongly depends on concept abstraction: SDCs excel at perceptually grounded descriptive concepts, whereas VLMs provide useful hypotheses for complex interpretative scenes. Finally, we find that enforcing explicit hierarchy within model architectures limits coverage compared to spatial feature aggregation. Overall, rather than competing approaches, SDCs and VLMs emerge as complementary components for future hybrid indexing systems combining structured retrieval with exploratory annotation assistance. As a methodological contribution, we define the soft F1 metric to provide a taxonomy-aware evaluation that credits semantically close predictions based on lowest common ancestors.

AI.tldr: The paper compares generative vision-language models with supervised discriminative classifiers for automated iconographic annotation of 9,735 medieval manuscript folio images labeled with 2,333 TIMEL concepts. ML-Decoder with Asymmetric Loss gives the strongest retrieval (precision@1 of 0.696, MRR of 0.806), while VLMs offer broader taxonomic coverage.
AI.motivation: Digitised medieval manuscripts create a growing need for automated iconographic indexing, and it is unclear how generative VLMs and supervised discriminative classifiers compare on this task.
AI.method: VLM experiments evaluate fine-tuning, structured JSON decoding, taxonomy-based candidate generation and deterministic reranking; discriminative experiments evaluate flat, hierarchy-aware and patch-attention heads over a frozen DINOv3 encoder; the authors also define a soft F1 metric that credits semantically close predictions based on lowest common ancestors.
AI.result: ML-Decoder achieves the strongest overall retrieval (precision@1 of 0.696, MRR of 0.806), with loss calibration via Asymmetric Loss as the main performance lever; verify-calibrate reranking of VLM outputs reaches hierarchical F1 of 0.559; SDCs give superior precision within a closed vocabulary and excel on perceptually grounded descriptive concepts, while VLMs provide useful hypotheses for complex interpretative scenes; enforcing explicit hierarchy in the architecture limits coverage compared with spatial feature aggregation.
AI.conclusion: SDCs and VLMs are complementary components for future hybrid indexing systems that combine structured retrieval with exploratory annotation assistance.

title: Geometry-Aware Trajectory State Modeling for Few-Shot Action Recognition
comment: This work is accepted by The IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV) 2027
summary: Few-shot action recognition (FSAR) requires representations that expose discriminative motion dynamics from only a few labeled videos. Recent trajectory-based methods leverage long-term point tracks for explicit temporal correspondence, but often treat trajectories as carriers of sampled visual features or summarize their motion with compact 2D displacement-based descriptors. We instead view an action as the ordered evolution of 2.5D trajectory states and their local geometric interactions. Based on this view, we introduce GeoTRAM, a geometry-aware trajectory state modeling framework for FSAR. GeoTRAM lifts sparse tracks into 2.5D trajectories, where StateMotion models ordered intra-trajectory state evolution and RelMotion captures state-conditioned local interactions through time-varying relative geometry and motion. Quality-filtered spectral sampling provides more reliable trajectory initialization; complementary semantic, motion, and depth cues are separately refined and preserved for joint spatio-temporal modeling; action-guided reweighting and top-$\rho$ trajectory selection support complementary frame- and trajectory-level matching. Experiments on five FSAR benchmarks demonstrate strong gains on the motion-centric Something-Something benchmarks while maintaining competitive performance on more appearance-driven benchmarks and a favorable accuracy--efficiency trade-off.

AI.tldr: GeoTRAM models an action as the ordered evolution of 2.5D trajectory states and their local geometric interactions for few-shot action recognition. It shows strong gains on motion-centric Something-Something benchmarks while remaining competitive on appearance-driven benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Recent trajectory-based few-shot action recognition methods treat point tracks as carriers of sampled visual features or summarize motion with compact 2D displacement descriptors, which limits how much motion dynamics can be captured from only a few labeled videos.
AI.method: Sparse tracks are lifted into 2.5D trajectories; StateMotion models ordered intra-trajectory state evolution, and RelMotion captures state-conditioned local interactions through time-varying relative geometry and motion; quality-filtered spectral sampling initializes trajectories, semantic, motion and depth cues are refined separately and then modeled jointly, and action-guided reweighting with top-rho trajectory selection supports frame- and trajectory-level matching.
AI.result: Experiments on five FSAR benchmarks show strong gains on the motion-centric Something-Something benchmarks, competitive performance on more appearance-driven benchmarks, and a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off.
AI.conclusion: Modeling geometry-aware trajectory state evolution is an effective representation for few-shot action recognition, particularly where motion is central.

title: Calibrating Track-Query Updates at Test Time for Multi-Object Tracking
summary: Multi-Object Tracking (MOT) requires localizing multiple objects and maintaining their identities over time. Recent query-propagation trackers carry target-specific representations across frames and update them with current-frame image features, yet identity association remains difficult when visually similar targets overlap or cross. During such interactions, current-frame query updates may contain components directed toward nearby active tracks, which may affect identity association in later frames. To investigate this issue, we analyze track-query updates preceding identity switches (IDSWs), where the same target is assigned a different track ID. Our analysis shows that (i) propagated track-query representations change more abruptly before IDSWs, (ii) current-frame updates have larger positive projections along directions toward other active tracks, and (iii) bounding-box intersection over union (IoU) retrieves the counterpart track involved in a subsequent IDSW with high recall when that track remains active before the switch. Motivated by these findings, we propose Test-time Track-Query Calibration (TQC), a training-free and gradient-free method for query-propagation trackers. TQC calibrates the tracker output before propagation using a bounded correction estimated from update components directed toward nearby active tracks. It requires only track-query representations and bounding boxes available during inference, without retraining or architectural modification. Across nine DanceTrack and SportsMOT test settings, TQC improves HOTA and AssA in all settings and IDF1 in eight, with an average HOTA gain of +0.38 and limited inference overhead. Controlled variants on six validation settings further show that TQC's correction direction yields more consistent HOTA improvements than alternative directions with matched correction norms.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes track-query updates preceding identity switches in query-propagation multi-object trackers and proposes Test-time Track-Query Calibration, a training-free and gradient-free correction. TQC improves HOTA and AssA in all nine DanceTrack and SportsMOT test settings, with an average HOTA gain of +0.38.
AI.motivation: Identity association in query-propagation trackers is difficult when visually similar targets overlap or cross, because current-frame query updates may contain components directed toward nearby active tracks, which can affect identity association in later frames.
AI.method: Analysis of updates preceding identity switches finds abrupt changes in propagated track queries, larger positive projections toward other active tracks, and IoU retrieving the counterpart track; TQC calibrates the tracker output before propagation using a bounded correction estimated from update components directed toward nearby active tracks, requiring only inference-time track-query representations and bounding boxes.
AI.result: Across nine DanceTrack and SportsMOT test settings, TQC improves HOTA and AssA in all settings and IDF1 in eight, with an average HOTA gain of +0.38 and limited inference overhead; controlled variants on six validation settings show that its correction direction yields more consistent HOTA improvements than alternative directions with matched correction norms.
AI.conclusion: Calibrating track-query updates at test time offers a lightweight way to reduce identity switches without retraining or architectural modification.

title: Vision-Based Density Estimation for Adaptive Traffic Control
summary: Traffic congestion is becoming a critical challenge in rapidly growing urban centers, particularly in developing nations where rapid urbanization and inadequate transport infrastructure place increasing strain on transport networks. In highly heterogeneous and chaotic traffic flows, camera-based traffic-state estimation is limited by severe vehicle occlusion and overlap. In this paper, we propose a framework to optimize traffic flow directly from stochastic visual observations. The architecture is structurally decoupled into three primary components: (a) vehicle density estimation, (b) predictive dynamics modeling, and (c) policy optimization. The proposed methodology introduces a convolutional neural network (CNN) that learns the mapping from camera feeds to spatial density maps, utilizing an adaptive k-nearest-neighbor (k-NN) Gaussian kernel to handle varying congestion levels. This feeds into an ST3DNet predictive module for spatiotemporal forecasting, followed by a hierarchical Graph-Transformer Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) algorithm to optimize signal phases. The density estimation stage was evaluated on 40 annotated intersection images from Rambagh 4, Jaipur, India, with a reported five-fold validation mean absolute error (MAE) of $3.32 \pm 0.95$ vehicles and a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 14.5%. These results pertain to the perception component; empirical training and evaluation of the forecasting and control stages remain future work.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a three-part framework that estimates vehicle density from camera feeds, forecasts traffic dynamics and optimizes signal phases with multi-agent reinforcement learning. Only the density estimation stage is evaluated, with a MAE of 3.32 +/- 0.95 vehicles and a MAPE of 14.5% on 40 intersection images.
AI.motivation: Camera-based traffic-state estimation in heterogeneous, chaotic traffic flows in rapidly urbanizing cities, particularly in developing nations, is limited by severe vehicle occlusion and overlap.
AI.method: A CNN maps camera feeds to spatial density maps using an adaptive k-nearest-neighbor Gaussian kernel to handle varying congestion levels; an ST3DNet module performs spatiotemporal forecasting; a hierarchical Graph-Transformer Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning algorithm optimizes signal phases.
AI.result: On 40 annotated intersection images from Rambagh 4, Jaipur, India, the density estimation stage gives five-fold validation MAE of 3.32 +/- 0.95 vehicles and MAPE of 14.5%; the forecasting and control stages have not yet been empirically trained or evaluated.
AI.conclusion: The reported results concern only the perception component, and empirical training and evaluation of forecasting and control remain future work.

title: Residual Motion Splatting for Continuous Space-Time Video Super-Resolution
summary: Continuous space-time video super-resolution produces a high-resolution, highframe-rate video from a low-resolution, low-frame-rate one at arbitrary spatial scales and temporal instants. Classical spatial multi-frame super-resolution has shown that detail beyond a single frame's sampling limit can be recovered by aligning complementary observations with sub-pixel precision and accumulating them on a finer grid. Existing learning-based methods largely depart from this principle: some align and fuse frames only at low resolution before regressing a continuous high-resolution representation, while others interpolate each frame to the output resolution before splatting. In both cases, the per-frame samples are resampled before fusion, so their sub-pixel positions are lost before frames are combined. Restoring this principle in a learned continuous model raises two challenges: estimating sub-pixel motion at unobserved times, and handling holes and occlusions when splatting a coarse grid onto a finer one. We address the first by predicting per-pixel continuous trajectories that refine linear optical-flow paths with smooth residual motion, using features integrated over the full video sequence. We address the second by directly splatting consecutive low-resolution features in a learned latent space onto a high-resolution grid at their predicted sub-pixel positions with predicted visibility weights, before a decoder resolves remaining ambiguities. This makes temporal interpolation and multi-frame superresolution a single operation. Our method improves both reconstruction fidelity and perceptual quality on multiple standard benchmarks over the state of the art, while running up to an order of magnitude faster.

AI.tldr: Residual Motion Splatting performs continuous space-time video super-resolution by predicting per-pixel continuous trajectories and splatting low-resolution features onto a high-resolution grid at sub-pixel positions. It improves reconstruction fidelity and perceptual quality over the state of the art while running up to an order of magnitude faster.
AI.motivation: Existing learned methods resample frames before fusion and so lose the sub-pixel positions that classical multi-frame super-resolution exploits by aligning observations with sub-pixel precision.
AI.method: Per-pixel continuous trajectories refine linear optical-flow paths with smooth residual motion, using features integrated over the full sequence; consecutive low-resolution features are splatted in a learned latent space onto a high-resolution grid at predicted sub-pixel positions with predicted visibility weights, and a decoder resolves remaining ambiguities, so temporal interpolation and multi-frame super-resolution become a single operation.
AI.result: On multiple standard benchmarks the method improves both reconstruction fidelity and perceptual quality over the state of the art, while running up to an order of magnitude faster.
AI.conclusion: Restoring the sub-pixel sampling principle inside a learned continuous model unifies temporal interpolation and multi-frame super-resolution into one operation.

title: UnMixMamba: Unmixing Guided State Space Subpixel Mapping of Crops from MODIS Time Series
summary: Subpixel mapping (SPM) of crop types from \SI{250}{m} Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) time series to field-scale Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada (AAFC) labels supports acreage estimation and agricultural monitoring. Three difficulties remain: (i)~spectral-temporal coupling and mixed pixels that break direct coarse-to-fine classifiers; (ii)~intra-class endmember variability that a single spectrum per crop cannot capture; and (iii)~uniform refinement on the high-resolution (HR) grid, which treats every subpixel the same, so most of the effort goes to easy pixels while errors remain in the minority class. UnMixMamba addresses them as follows. For~(i), a temporal-spectral-spatial decoupled (TSSD) factorization estimates simplex fractions and drives AAFC classification from the same mixture field, instead of mapping low-resolution (LR) observations directly to HR logits. For~(ii), \(\times 8\) abundance super-resolution and a learnable per-crop variant endmember bank reconstruct the MODIS cube at LR and HR under a linear mixing model. For~(iii), the predicted crop fractions decide where a fixed Mamba token budget is spent, so HR refinement focuses on the minority class instead of the full grid. On Alberta 2015 under a fixed spatial-block protocol, UnMixMamba reaches OA 0.8397, mIoU 0.6640, AA 0.7837, and Kappa 0.7715, ahead of ST-DRes, ESPCN, FineCrop, AgriFM, and classical SPM baselines. The task is closed-set four-crop mapping inside a known agricultural mask.

AI.tldr: UnMixMamba performs subpixel mapping of four crop types from 250 m MODIS time series to field-scale AAFC labels using a Mamba-based design. On Alberta 2015 under a fixed spatial-block protocol it reaches OA 0.8397 and mIoU 0.6640, ahead of ST-DRes, ESPCN, FineCrop, AgriFM and classical SPM baselines.
AI.motivation: Subpixel crop mapping from coarse MODIS data faces spectral-temporal coupling and mixed pixels, intra-class endmember variability that a single spectrum per crop cannot capture, and uniform refinement on the high-resolution grid that spends effort on easy pixels while minority-class errors remain.
AI.method: A temporal-spectral-spatial decoupled factorization estimates simplex fractions and drives AAFC classification from the same mixture field; x8 abundance super-resolution and a learnable per-crop variant endmember bank reconstruct the MODIS cube at low and high resolution under a linear mixing model; predicted crop fractions decide where a fixed Mamba token budget is spent, so high-resolution refinement focuses on the minority class.
AI.result: On Alberta 2015 under a fixed spatial-block protocol, OA 0.8397, mIoU 0.6640, AA 0.7837 and Kappa 0.7715, ahead of ST-DRes, ESPCN, FineCrop, AgriFM and classical SPM baselines; the task is closed-set four-crop mapping inside a known agricultural mask.
AI.conclusion: Allocating a fixed refinement budget according to predicted crop fractions targets minority-class errors in subpixel crop mapping, within the closed-set four-crop setting evaluated.

title: The Power Watershed as a Differentiable Segmentation Layer
summary: Can a Watershed transform, the classical tool of morphological segmentation, be placed at the end of a deep network and trained through? The Power Watershed (PW) is the limit of the seeded Random Walker (RW) as p grows to infinity with edge weights raised to the power p. At every finite p the RW solves a sparse positive-definite linear system and is exactly differentiable with respect to the edge weights and the unaries through one adjoint solve; its multi-label form costs one right-hand side per label, and its limit is the PW. We study this family as the last layer of a segmentation network, the watershed layer (WS layer). A conditioning study measures how the solve, the gradient and the distance to the limit evolve with p, and the implicit gradient is checked against unrolling. On synthetic data with correct edge costs the WS layer transforms a soft prediction into an exact boundary. On nuclei segmentation (PanNuke), a binary WS layer is level with a thresholded U-Net. With the instances as labels, the WS layer turns the U-Net into an instance segmenter whose number of labels is set per image by the markers rather than by the output layout, and the network is trained through that partition: instance F1 score rises from 0.656 to 0.795 over a U-Net with connected components, level with the same network followed by a tuned marker watershed. At the training temperature the partition is a watershed of the learned costs, and the finite temperature lets the solve hedge, discounting weak markers and sharing contested pixels. The hedging puts the WS layer 0.015--0.020 F1 ahead of the baseline when trained on a tenth of the data, at the price of having to deploy the finite-p solve rather than its exact limit at inference. Code and the full experimental record are released.

AI.tldr: The paper turns the Power Watershed, the infinite-power limit of the seeded Random Walker, into a differentiable watershed layer for segmentation networks. On PanNuke nuclei segmentation, the layer raises instance F1 from 0.656 to 0.795 over a U-Net with connected components.
AI.motivation: The classical watershed transform is a morphological segmentation tool that cannot be trained through, so a differentiable formulation is needed to place it at the end of a deep network.
AI.method: At every finite power p the Random Walker solves a sparse positive-definite linear system and is exactly differentiable with respect to edge weights and unaries through one adjoint solve; its multi-label form costs one right-hand side per label; the watershed layer uses this family as the last layer of a segmentation network, with a conditioning study of the solve, gradient and distance to the limit as p varies, and implicit gradients checked against unrolling.
AI.result: On synthetic data with correct edge costs the layer turns a soft prediction into an exact boundary; on PanNuke a binary layer is level with a thresholded U-Net; with instances as labels, instance F1 rises from 0.656 to 0.795 over a U-Net with connected components, level with the same network followed by a tuned marker watershed; at finite temperature the solve hedges, placing the layer 0.015 to 0.020 F1 ahead of the baseline when trained on a tenth of the data, at the price of deploying the finite-p solve rather than its exact limit at inference.
AI.conclusion: Training through the watershed partition lets the network set its label count from markers and hedge against weak markers, at the cost of running the finite-p solve at inference.

title: Detecting Fine-Grained Differences between Image Datasets
summary: Detecting whether and in particular how two data distributions differ is a fundamental statistical problem. For example, we might be interested in which concepts (expressed in natural language) differ between two classes, the outputs of different generative models, or the same model with different prompt specifications. When working with large and complex image datasets, we intuitively think that first selecting concepts from a broad list using fine-grained patch embeddings, and then optimizing the concepts to better fit the data is an effective workflow. However, prior work instead uses MLLMs to propose concepts and image-level embeddings to select them. Therefore, we systematically compare these techniques and find that selecting concepts from broad lists can replace MLLM-proposals at obviously lower cost. MLLM inference can then be spent on optimizing selected concepts instead to achieve substantial improvements. Additionally, by designing a new benchmark that focuses on low-prevalence and multi-concept distinctions, we find that selecting nonredundant concepts instead of only the most distinguishing concepts matters, and we introduce techniques for how to effectively do this. Finally, we show how our methods address important problems like detecting spurious correlations and biases. Overall, our work presents a fundamental perspective shift on how we analyze interpretable distributional differences between datasets.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that selecting concepts from broad lists using fine-grained patch embeddings can replace MLLM-proposed concepts at lower cost, with MLLM inference better spent on optimizing the selected concepts. It also introduces a benchmark for low-prevalence, multi-concept distinctions between image datasets.
AI.motivation: Detecting how two data distributions differ is a fundamental statistical problem, but prior work uses MLLMs to propose concepts and image-level embeddings to select them, and the authors argue this is costly and that a first-select-then-optimize workflow is more effective.
AI.method: The authors systematically compare concept selection from broad lists using fine-grained patch embeddings against MLLM proposal, spend MLLM inference on optimizing the selected concepts, design a new benchmark focused on low-prevalence and multi-concept distinctions, and introduce techniques for selecting nonredundant concepts.
AI.result: Selecting from broad lists can replace MLLM proposals at obviously lower cost, and MLLM inference spent on optimizing selected concepts yields substantial improvements; on the new benchmark, selecting nonredundant concepts matters more than selecting only the most distinguishing ones; the methods address detecting spurious correlations and biases.
AI.conclusion: The work offers a shift in perspective on how interpretable distributional differences between image datasets are analyzed.

title: RoSAMDepth: Robust Self-supervised Depth Estimation Leveraging Segment Anything Model
comment: 13 pages, 8 figures, including supplementary material. Published in CVPR 2026
summary: Robust depth estimation aims to maintain high-quality depths across diverse conditions. However, most existing methods estimate depth without taking into account the object-level information. As a result, the predicted depth may easily deviate within objects and become blurred under adverse conditions. To overcome this weakness, we propose RoSAMDepth, a novel framework that can assist robust self-supervised depth estimation in leveraging rich and diverse object-level priors from the Segment Anything Model (SAM). We focus on incorporating object-level information across three key aspects: a segment-guided representation contrasting method that injects object-level awareness into the feature representation space; an adaptive regional outlier masking strategy combined with a regional Gaussian likelihood loss that enforces regional depth smoothness; and an object-level reliability estimation strategy that mitigates the influence of unreliable supervision. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets and diverse weather conditions demonstrate that our method produces sharper, more accurate depth predictions, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Our code is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: RoSAMDepth is a robust self-supervised depth estimation framework that injects object-level priors from the Segment Anything Model. It produces sharper, more accurate depth predictions and consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across multiple datasets and diverse weather conditions.
AI.motivation: Most depth estimation methods ignore object-level information, so predicted depth can deviate within objects and become blurred under adverse conditions.
AI.method: Three components: a segment-guided representation contrasting method that injects object-level awareness into the feature space; an adaptive regional outlier masking strategy combined with a regional Gaussian likelihood loss that enforces regional depth smoothness; and an object-level reliability estimation strategy that mitigates the influence of unreliable supervision.
AI.result: Extensive experiments across multiple datasets and diverse weather conditions show sharper, more accurate depth predictions, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art methods.
AI.conclusion: Object-level priors from SAM improve the robustness of self-supervised depth estimation under adverse conditions.

title: SpectralTF-MAE: A Pre-trained Spectral Foundation Model for Tokamak Fusion Plasma Diagnostics
summary: Spectroscopic diagnostics provide rich information for characterizing plasma states in tokamak fusion experiments, while existing learning-based approaches are often designed for individual tasks and rely heavily on labeled data. In this work, we propose SpectralTF-MAE, a self-supervised spectral foundation model for tokamak plasma diagnostics. The model is pretrained on paired charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy (CXRS) and X-ray crystal spectroscopy (XCS) measurements through masked spectral reconstruction. To better capture diagnostically important spectral structures, we introduce a peak-aware masking strategy together with a peak-enhanced reconstruction objective, encouraging the model to focus on characteristic spectral regions. A shared Transformer encoder is employed to learn transferable representations across different diagnostic modalities. The pretrained model is further adapted to several downstream tasks, including plasma-parameter prediction, cross-diagnostic spectral generation, and spectral peak analysis. Experiments on EAST diagnostic data demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves competitive performance across different tasks and consistently benefits from self-supervised spectral pretraining. These results indicate the potential of SpectralTF-MAE as a general and transferable representation learning framework for plasma spectroscopic diagnostics.

AI.tldr: SpectralTF-MAE is a self-supervised spectral foundation model pretrained on paired charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy and X-ray crystal spectroscopy measurements from tokamak plasmas via masked spectral reconstruction. It is adapted to plasma-parameter prediction, cross-diagnostic spectral generation and spectral peak analysis on EAST data with competitive performance.
AI.motivation: Learning-based spectroscopic diagnostics for tokamak fusion plasmas are often designed for individual tasks and rely heavily on labeled data.
AI.method: Masked spectral reconstruction pretraining on paired CXRS and XCS measurements, with a peak-aware masking strategy and a peak-enhanced reconstruction objective that focuses the model on characteristic spectral regions, and a shared Transformer encoder that learns representations across diagnostic modalities.
AI.result: On EAST diagnostic data the framework achieves competitive performance across different tasks and consistently benefits from self-supervised spectral pretraining.
AI.conclusion: SpectralTF-MAE shows potential as a general and transferable representation learning framework for plasma spectroscopic diagnostics.

title: Data Scaling Laws in Stereo Matching: From In-domain Fitting to Cross-domain Generalization
summary: In the era of large models, stereo matching is developing towards generalizable foundation models trained on million-scale synthetic images. However, how model performance scales up with synthetic data is still underexplored. In this work, we preliminarily investigate the in-domain and cross-domain data scaling laws in stereo matching. A realistic synthetic dataset, named XStereo, containing 200 thousand samples is first built to serve as a high-quality benchmark for data scaling research. In-domain training on five large-scale datasets demonstrate a two-regime scaling behavior with data, transitioning from the standard power law to saturation, where the critical transition point is approximately invariant under a fixed model. Cross-domain performance exhibits a substantially weaker and less predictable dependence on the source-domain data scale. The distribution and coverage diversity are more effective for diminishing domain gaps. More instructive suggestions are provided for high-efficiency data construction and training. The insightful findings are significant verification and extension of the existing scaling laws in both language and vision, paving the way to efficient and stronger stereo matching. The XStereo dataset is public at this https URL.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates in-domain and cross-domain data scaling laws for stereo matching and builds XStereo, a 200K-sample synthetic benchmark. In-domain performance follows a two-regime scaling curve that saturates, while cross-domain performance depends more weakly and less predictably on source-domain data scale.
AI.motivation: Stereo matching is moving toward generalizable foundation models trained on million-scale synthetic images, yet how model performance scales with synthetic data is still underexplored.
AI.method: A realistic synthetic dataset, XStereo, containing 200 thousand samples is built as a benchmark for data scaling research; in-domain training on five large-scale datasets studies scaling, and cross-domain experiments study the effect of source-domain data scale and diversity.
AI.result: In-domain training shows two-regime scaling, transitioning from a standard power law to saturation at a critical point that is approximately invariant under a fixed model; cross-domain performance has a substantially weaker and less predictable dependence on source-domain data scale; distribution and coverage diversity are more effective for diminishing domain gaps.
AI.conclusion: The findings verify and extend existing scaling laws in language and vision and give guidance for efficient data construction and training in stereo matching.

title: V-CAPE: Visual Consistency Assessment for Product Image Editing
summary: Recent advances in generative image editing enable complex transformations such as background replacement, object manipulation, and pose adjustment from natural language instructions.
