AI.motivation: In thinking VLMs the bottleneck for high-resolution detail is selecting evidence rather than seeing it, and the focus of localization heads fades as reasoning grows, while outcome rewards give no signal about where to look.
AI.method: Localization-Head Alignment makes attention a training signal: whenever the reasoning states a visual fact, the localization heads are trained to attend to the focal region rather than the background, as an auxiliary loss in both SFT and RL training.
AI.result: On V*, HR-Bench 4K and TreeBench, LHA lifts Qwen3.5-4B from 74.1% to 76.6%, the best single-pass 4B result evaluated and ahead of multi-pass zooming methods and released 7B models. Alignment alone adds 1.8 points over otherwise identical training while shortening reasoning by 20%, and the gains carry over to Qwen2.5-VL-3B. Ablating four localization heads costs 13.2 points more than ablating four random heads.
AI.conclusion: Supervising attention on localization heads improves fine-grained perception and shortens reasoning in thinking VLMs without extra inference passes.

title: AB-Attention: Accurate Block Attention for Accelerating Video Diffusion Transformers
summary: Video diffusion transformers generate high-quality videos, but the quadratic cost of 3D full attention dominates their inference. Dynamic block-sparse attention reduces this cost by computing exact attention only on key/value blocks selected from current activations. However, its fidelity degrades under aggressive sparsity: blocks are scored from coarse summaries or formed by costly global clustering, pruned blocks vanish from the softmax, and whole tiles are kept or dropped even when only a few of their keys matter. To address these limitations, we propose Accurate Block Attention (AB-Attention), a training-free method that accurately approximates dense attention at high sparsity. Its Intra-Block Clustering Selector (IBCS) estimates block importance faithfully yet cheaply by clustering queries only within each query block, without permuting tokens. Sampling with Inclusion-Probability Weighting (SIP) then samples blocks in proportion to these estimates and reweights them by inverse inclusion probability, so that one pass estimates dense attention rather than truncating it. Finally, its kernel gathers key/value blocks much smaller than a tile into full tensor-core tiles, refining selection at no extra tensor-core cost. On Wan2.1 and HunyuanVideo, AB-Attention skips 89--92\% of attention, whereas the baselines compute 1.8--3.6$\times$ as much, yet it still improves PSNR by up to 4.4~dB over the strongest baseline and achieves up to 2.23$\times$ end-to-end speedup. Our code is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: AB-Attention is a training-free sparse attention method for video diffusion transformers that skips 89 to 92 percent of attention while approximating dense attention more accurately, with up to 2.23x end-to-end speedup.
AI.motivation: Dynamic block-sparse attention loses fidelity at high sparsity because block scoring is coarse or costly, pruned blocks vanish from the softmax, and whole tiles are kept or dropped even when only a few of their keys matter.
AI.method: The Intra-Block Clustering Selector estimates block importance by clustering queries within each query block without permuting tokens. Sampling with Inclusion-Probability Weighting samples blocks in proportion to these estimates and reweights them by inverse inclusion probability, so one pass estimates dense attention. A kernel gathers key/value blocks much smaller than a tile into full tensor-core tiles.
AI.result: On Wan2.1 and HunyuanVideo, AB-Attention skips 89 to 92 percent of attention, whereas the baselines compute 1.8 to 3.6 times as much. It improves PSNR by up to 4.4 dB over the strongest baseline and achieves up to 2.23x end-to-end speedup.
AI.conclusion: Accurate block selection with inverse inclusion-probability reweighting enables high sparsity in video diffusion transformers without any training.

title: EditAgent: Rethinking Agentic Image Editing
summary: Agentic image editors decompose complex requests into steps, but when a step fails, they mostly retry with the same narrow set of tools and a judge that scores each output by eye directly. We argue that such agents are bounded by two spaces: the action space of what the agent can do, and the observation space of what its judge can see. On our expert-annotated benchmark, a general-purpose editor yields no usable result in over 40% of the cases, and no judge is reliable across edit types. We present EditAgent, which expands both spaces. It routes each step to general editors and specialized methods, and attaches to each candidate a verification record. With these records, off-the-shelf VLM judges outperform finetuned reward models. Candidates are generated in parallel and judged in one listwise call: experts prefer this to sequential refinement in 78.5% of decided comparisons, at no more than half the judge calls. EditAgent improves two open-weight editors on three benchmarks and serves as a data engine for training stronger editors.

AI.tldr: EditAgent expands the action and observation spaces of agentic image editing by routing steps to general and specialized editors and attaching verification records to candidates, so off-the-shelf VLM judges outperform finetuned reward models.
AI.motivation: Agentic editors retry failed steps with a narrow tool set and a judge that scores outputs by eye, which bounds them by their action and observation spaces; on the expert-annotated benchmark a general-purpose editor yields no usable result in over 40% of cases.
AI.method: EditAgent routes each step to general editors and specialized methods and attaches a verification record to each candidate. Candidates are generated in parallel and judged together in one listwise call.
AI.result: Experts prefer listwise judging to sequential refinement in 78.5% of decided comparisons, at no more than half the judge calls. EditAgent improves two open-weight editors on three benchmarks, and with the verification records off-the-shelf VLM judges outperform finetuned reward models.
AI.conclusion: Expanding what the agent can do and what the judge can see yields better image editing, and EditAgent also serves as a data engine for training stronger editors.

title: DEQ-Stereo: Deep Euilibrium Video Stereo Matching via Adaptive Convergence
summary: Iterative refinement models have significantly improved stereo matching accuracy, but their rigid, fixed update schedules incur heavy computational costs and a strict trade-off between speed and accuracy. This challenge is magnified in video streams, where traditional online methods resort to reducing feature channels or relying on expensive temporal warping. To address this, we propose \textbf{DEQ-Stereo}, a novel video stereo matching framework based on the Deep Equilibrium (DEQ) paradigm. Instead of unrolling a fixed number of iterations, DEQ-Stereo reformulates the refinement as an implicit fixed-point problem, adaptively terminating once convergence is met. To ensure fast and stable intra-frame convergence, we introduce the \textbf{Convolutional Simplified Gated Unit (ConvSGU)}, which eliminates unnecessary non-linearities by modeling the latent state as a gated, element-wise sum of inputs. Furthermore, to exploit cross-frame temporal coherence, we propose \textbf{Temporal State Transfer (TST)}, a warm-start strategy that propagates the converged hidden state to the next frame without requiring explicit pose or warping priors. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that DEQ-Stereo delivers state-of-the-art performance with a superior accuracy-to-latency trade-off.

AI.tldr: DEQ-Stereo reformulates iterative video stereo matching as an implicit fixed-point problem that terminates adaptively and warm-starts across frames, reaching state-of-the-art performance with a better accuracy-to-latency trade-off.
AI.motivation: Iterative refinement with fixed update schedules is computationally costly and carries a strict speed-accuracy trade-off, and video methods either reduce feature channels or rely on expensive temporal warping.
AI.method: Refinement is formulated with the Deep Equilibrium paradigm and terminates once convergence is met. ConvSGU models the latent state as a gated, element-wise sum of inputs without unnecessary non-linearities. Temporal State Transfer propagates the converged hidden state to the next frame as a warm start, without requiring pose or warping priors.
AI.result: Extensive evaluations show state-of-the-art performance with a superior accuracy-to-latency trade-off. The abstract gives no specific numerical results.
AI.conclusion: Adaptive fixed-point convergence combined with temporal warm starts provides an efficient route to accurate video stereo matching.

title: Confidence Filtering in Video-Based Gait Assessment: Measurement Error versus Selection Shift
comment: 6 pages + 2-page appendix, 4 figures, 2 supplementary figures, 2 tables. Submitted to the 2027 IEEE International Conference on Rehabilitation Robotics (ICORR)
summary: Video-based gait assessment often keeps only high-confidence pose observations, which can lower measurement error but change the movement assessed. We compared confidence selection with budget-matched random selection in a Parkinson-related cohort (n = 96) and an NF2-related replication cohort (n = 18). In the Parkinson-related cohort, confidence selection produced a small but consistent shift in the observed movement summary (+0.05 SD, 95% CI 0.03 to 0.07), while held-out Mini-BESTest error stayed flat (-0.04 points, -0.13 to 0.05); a policy preserving motion-group proportions reduced the shift, while NF2 showed no shift and its predictor did not beat a constant baseline. Because this shift mixes measurement error with selection shift, we decompose and simulate both on the cohort's window structure. Filtering lowers local error when error depends on confidence, but biases the endpoint once confidence tracks movement more than error. In the Parkinson-related data, confidence was only weakly tied to movement (rho = 0.14). There, filtering is harmless if well-tracked windows are unbiased. If instead systematic error only redistributes within participants, filtering can add up to 0.58 degrees. Unchanged clinical error from such small-cohort predictors therefore cannot show that quality filtering preserves the assessed movement.

AI.tldr: In video-based gait assessment, confidence filtering of pose observations shifts the movement being assessed even when it lowers measurement error, so clinical error alone cannot show that quality filtering preserves the movement.
AI.motivation: Keeping only high-confidence pose observations can lower measurement error but may change the movement that is assessed, and this selection shift has not been separated from measurement error.
AI.method: Confidence selection is compared with budget-matched random selection in a Parkinson-related cohort (n = 96) and an NF2-related replication cohort (n = 18). The shift and the error are decomposed and simulated on the cohort's window structure, and a policy that preserves motion-group proportions is tested.
AI.result: In the Parkinson-related cohort, confidence selection produces a small but consistent shift (+0.05 SD, 95% CI 0.03 to 0.07) while held-out Mini-BESTest error stays flat (-0.04 points, 95% CI -0.13 to 0.05). A proportion-preserving policy reduces the shift. NF2 shows no shift, and its predictor does not beat a constant baseline. Confidence is only weakly tied to movement (rho = 0.14), and filtering can add up to 0.58 degrees of bias if systematic error redistributes within participants.
AI.conclusion: Unchanged clinical error from small-cohort predictors cannot establish that quality filtering preserves the assessed movement.

title: NIF: Normal-Intersection Fields for Geometrically Consistent Oriented Box Refinement
summary: Accurate oriented detection requires a box to follow object boundaries, yet a standard regression head predicts its center, size, and angle from a pooled region representation. Small errors in these coupled parameters can displace long boundaries even when the object is correctly classified. We propose NIF, a refinement module that replaces an additional box regressor with normal-intersection fields. Given a coarse oriented box, the module observes local features at 20 boundary anchors and predicts signed distances along their outward normals. These observations admit an exact affine representation in five geometric variables. A differentiable, reliability-weighted least-squares fit projects the predicted field onto this representation and analytically recovers a refined rectangle. Tangential pooling preserves the normal position profile, while shared projection limits the added network to 0.132M parameters. On DOTA-v1.0, NIF reaches 78.00%, 79.11%, and 79.02% mAP with Oriented R-CNN, LSKNet-S, and Strip R-CNN, respectively, achieving the highest single-scale SOTA result in Table 1. It reaches 68.19% on DIOR-R, improves matched FAIR1M/DIOR-R baselines by 0.30/0.68%, and raises HRSC mean IoU from 0.867 to 0.888 while reducing field error by 24.5%. Across four different detector frameworks with the detectors frozen, relative AP75 improves by 1.57-4.18% and COCO-style mAP by 0.42-3.74%, without detector retraining. Code is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: NIF refines oriented boxes by fitting normal-intersection fields at 20 boundary anchors with a differentiable weighted least-squares solve, reaching 78.00% to 79.11% mAP on DOTA-v1.0 across detectors while adding only 0.132M parameters.
AI.motivation: Standard regression heads predict center, size and angle jointly from pooled region features, so small errors in these coupled parameters can displace long object boundaries even when the object is correctly classified.
AI.method: A refinement module replaces an extra box regressor with normal-intersection fields. From a coarse oriented box it observes local features at 20 boundary anchors and predicts signed distances along their outward normals. These observations admit an exact affine representation in five geometric variables, and a differentiable, reliability-weighted least-squares fit analytically recovers a refined rectangle. Tangential pooling and shared projection keep the added network small.
AI.result: On DOTA-v1.0, NIF reaches 78.00%, 79.11% and 79.02% mAP with Oriented R-CNN, LSKNet-S and Strip R-CNN, the highest single-scale SOTA result in the paper's Table 1. It reaches 68.19% on DIOR-R, improves matched FAIR1M and DIOR-R baselines by 0.30 and 0.68%, and raises HRSC mean IoU from 0.867 to 0.888 while cutting field error by 24.5%. With frozen detectors across four frameworks, relative AP75 improves by 1.57 to 4.18% and COCO-style mAP by 0.42 to 3.74%.
AI.conclusion: Geometrically structured boundary refinement improves oriented detection across different frameworks without detector retraining.

title: WorldProbe: When Video World Models Fall Apart under Long-Horizon Spatial Exploration
summary: Video world models generate future visual observations from camera or action inputs, with the goal of synthesizing persistent 3D worlds that can be explored across time and space. Existing benchmarks typically evaluate short interactions or rely on camera trajectories fixed before generation. The performance of video world models under long-horizon exploration with extensive camera motion remains under-explored. We introduce WorldProbe, a diagnostic benchmark that uses a goal-conditioned multimodal agent to adapt camera actions online during generation. WorldProbe comprises 164 test cases across four probing families. Across 10 state-of-the-art models, we generate more than 1,600 rollouts totaling approximately 800 minutes, with horizons up to 180 seconds. Our evaluation across four dimensions reveals both the degradation of local measures and the emergence of long-range inconsistencies. We find that recent models sustain visual and content quality for longer, while long-range memory and evolution remain weak. These results expose a gap between locally stable generation and persistent world consistency that is largely missed by existing benchmarks. Code and benchmark resources are available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: WorldProbe is a diagnostic benchmark that uses a goal-conditioned multimodal agent to adapt camera actions online, showing that video world models keep local quality for longer but lose long-range consistency over horizons up to 180 seconds.
AI.motivation: Existing benchmarks evaluate short interactions or camera trajectories fixed before generation, leaving the performance of video world models under long-horizon exploration with extensive camera motion under-explored.
AI.method: WorldProbe comprises 164 test cases across four probing families, and an agent adapts camera actions online during generation. Across 10 state-of-the-art models, more than 1,600 rollouts totaling about 800 minutes were generated, with horizons up to 180 seconds, and evaluated on four dimensions.
AI.result: The evaluation reveals degradation of local measures and the emergence of long-range inconsistencies. Recent models sustain visual and content quality for longer, while long-range memory and evolution remain weak.
AI.conclusion: A gap exists between locally stable generation and persistent world consistency, a gap that existing benchmarks largely miss.

title: Cross-Encoder Anchor Refinement for Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection
summary: Zero-shot anomaly detection aims to transfer anomaly discrimination from auxiliary training domains to unseen categories while localizing subtle defects. A key challenge is to construct discriminative references that combine contextual representations with complementary local evidence. We present Cross-Encoder Anchor Refinement (CEAR), which connects two visual encoding paths for the same image at the anchor stage, before normal and anomalous prototypes are constructed. An independent convolutional encoder pretrained for industrial product recognition builds an image-specific memory shared across selected vision transformer (ViT) layers. Spatial anchors read from ViT patch features query this memory through cross-attention and undergo residual refinement. Image-conditioned normal and anomalous queries then gate anchor aggregation to construct prototypes for anomaly scoring. Across 13 industrial and medical datasets, CEAR achieves the best performance in 57 of 68 evaluations spanning image-level detection and pixel-level localization. Notably, CEAR surpasses all other state-of-the-art methods in 41 of 44 pixel-level comparisons. Across 11 localization datasets, mean gains in pixel-level maximum F1 score and average precision are 4.45 and 3.79 percentage points, respectively. This study shows how cross-encoder interaction at the anchor stage can integrate complementary visual representations for fine-grained anomaly localization across domains.

AI.tldr: CEAR is a zero-shot anomaly detection method that connects two visual encoding paths at the anchor stage, refining ViT patch anchors against an industrial CNN memory before prototypes are built. It achieves the best performance in 57 of 68 evaluations across 13 industrial and medical datasets.
AI.motivation: Zero-shot anomaly detection must transfer to unseen categories and localize subtle defects, but building discriminative references that combine contextual representations with complementary local evidence is difficult.
AI.method: An independent convolutional encoder pretrained for industrial product recognition builds an image-specific memory shared across selected ViT layers. Spatial anchors from ViT patch features query this memory through cross-attention with residual refinement, and image-conditioned normal and anomalous queries gate anchor aggregation into prototypes for anomaly scoring.
AI.result: CEAR achieves the best performance in 57 of 68 evaluations spanning image-level detection and pixel-level localization, and surpasses all other state-of-the-art methods in 41 of 44 pixel-level comparisons. Across 11 localization datasets, mean gains in pixel-level maximum F1 score and average precision are 4.45 and 3.79 percentage points.
AI.conclusion: Cross-encoder interaction at the anchor stage can integrate complementary visual representations for fine-grained anomaly localization across domains.

title: SCOPE: Semantic COdec Pre-Editing for Object-Preserving Compression
summary: Image compression is increasingly used before machine vision systems, yet standard codecs are mainly optimized for human perception rather than downstream task accuracy. We propose SCOPE (Semantic COdec Pre-Editing), a conditional image pre-editor that modifies images before compression to improve the bitrate and detection accuracy trade-off. The model is conditioned on the codec family and compression severity, allowing a single trained network to adapt to multiple compression settings without retraining or loading codec-specific weights. Instead of uniformly preserving the whole image, the pre-editor learns to protect task-relevant regions while simplifying less important background content to improve compressibility. The resulting rate-accuracy curves show consistent gains across different codec families and detector architectures, together with strong transferability to unseen learned and wavelet-based compression families.

AI.tldr: SCOPE is a conditional image pre-editor that modifies images before compression so that task-relevant regions are preserved and background is simplified, improving the bitrate and detection accuracy trade-off for machine vision. A single network adapts to multiple codec families and compression severities.
AI.motivation: Standard codecs are optimized for human perception rather than downstream task accuracy, and uniformly preserving the whole image spends bits on content that matters little to the detector.
AI.method: The pre-editor is conditioned on codec family and compression severity and learns to protect task-relevant regions while simplifying less important background, without retraining or loading codec-specific weights.
AI.result: Rate-accuracy curves show consistent gains across different codec families and detector architectures, together with strong transferability to unseen learned and wavelet-based compression families.
AI.conclusion: Task-aware pre-editing before compression is a practical way to improve machine-vision accuracy at a given bitrate, with one model covering multiple codecs.

title: Aligning Medical Vision Language Models at the Capability Boundary with Entropy Adaptive Rubric Grounding
comment: Accepted at ACM Multimedia Asia 2026 (MMAsia 2026). 10 pages, 4 figures
summary: Medical diagnostic reasoning requires verifiable links between visual evidence and clinical knowledge, yet current medical vision language models are aligned with objectives that reward the wrong behavior. Uniform supervised fine tuning lets easy cases dominate updates while clinically critical boundary cases saturate prematurely. Sparse rewards based only on final-answer correctness cannot assess anatomical grounding or clinical logic, inviting reward hacking through answer shortcuts. We propose MedCBR, a two-stage alignment framework coupling boundary-aware preference optimization with rubric-grounded reinforcement learning. First, we construct counterfactual boundary preferences at the model's capability frontier using empirical pass rates and preference pairs that share reasoning prefixes but diverge at decisive diagnostic branches. Difficulty Weighted Boundary Preference Optimization (DBPO) concentrates learning on this calibrated boundary region. Second, we distill reusable clinical rubrics from boundary trajectories and activate them according to prediction entropy. Entropy Gated Grounded Policy Optimization (EGPO) rewards answer correctness, anatomical grounding, and reasoning fidelity while suppressing rubric noise on reliable samples. A reference policy anchored to the boundary-aligned model couples population-level boundary priors with instance-level uncertainty, making diagnostic reasoning more accurate and clinically grounded. Experiments on six medical benchmarks show consistent improvements over strong general, specialized, and reinforcement learning baselines, reaching 61.2% average accuracy with the largest gains on challenging differential diagnosis tasks. Ablations show super-additive gains: combining the two stages exceeds the sum of their individual improvements.

AI.tldr: MedCBR is a two-stage alignment framework for medical vision language models that combines boundary-aware preference optimization with rubric-grounded reinforcement learning. It reaches 61.2% average accuracy on six medical benchmarks, with the largest gains on differential diagnosis tasks.
AI.motivation: Uniform supervised fine tuning lets easy cases dominate updates while clinically critical boundary cases saturate, and final-answer-only rewards cannot assess anatomical grounding or clinical logic, which invites reward hacking through answer shortcuts.
AI.method: Counterfactual boundary preferences are built at the model's capability frontier using empirical pass rates, and DBPO concentrates learning on this boundary region. Clinical rubrics distilled from boundary trajectories are activated by prediction entropy in EGPO, which rewards answer correctness, anatomical grounding and reasoning fidelity while suppressing rubric noise on reliable samples.
AI.result: MedCBR shows consistent improvements over general, specialized and reinforcement learning baselines on six medical benchmarks, reaching 61.2% average accuracy, with the largest gains on challenging differential diagnosis tasks. Ablations show super-additive gains, so combining the two stages exceeds the sum of their individual improvements.
AI.conclusion: Coupling boundary-focused preference learning with entropy-gated rubric rewards yields more accurate and clinically grounded diagnostic reasoning than either stage alone.

title: LiDAR-SHIELD: A Fully Dockerized Adversarial Robustness Assessment Framework for LiDAR-Based 3D Perception Models
summary: LiDAR-based 3D perception underpins autonomous driving and robotics, yet deploying these models safely requires stress-testing them against adversarial inputs before real-world use. Although state-of-the-art adversarial attacks exist, their implementations are often fragmented across individual repositories, each tied to a specific architecture or task and requiring manual environment reconstruction and model-specific integration code. We present LIDARSHIELD, a unified and fully Dockerized framework that reverses this workflow: rather than installing the target model inside the toolkit, LIDARSHIELD exposes any model through three lightweight HTTP endpoints, namely /info, /forward, and /gradient As a result, connecting a new model or dataset requires only a single loader function or adapter. The framework supports both 3D semantic segmentation and 3D object detection through the same engine-service protocol, integrating a task-aware suite of state-of-the-art attacks, including PGD and Square Attack for segmentation, and point perturbation, point removal, point injection, and LiDAttack for detection. This enables systematic exposure of corner cases and vulnerabilities across heterogeneous LiDAR backbones. The LiDAR-Shield codebase is publicly available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: LIDARSHIELD is a unified, fully Dockerized framework for adversarial robustness assessment of LiDAR-based 3D perception models. It exposes any model through three HTTP endpoints, so connecting a new model or dataset requires only a single loader function or adapter.
AI.motivation: Adversarial attacks on LiDAR perception models are fragmented across individual repositories, each tied to a specific architecture or task and requiring manual environment reconstruction and model-specific integration code.
AI.method: The framework reverses the usual workflow: the target model is wrapped behind /info, /forward and /gradient endpoints rather than installed into the toolkit. It supports 3D semantic segmentation and 3D object detection through a common engine-service protocol, with PGD and Square Attack for segmentation and point perturbation, point removal, point injection and LiDAttack for detection.
AI.result: The abstract reports no quantitative results. It states that the framework enables systematic exposure of corner cases and vulnerabilities across heterogeneous LiDAR backbones, and that the codebase is publicly available.
AI.conclusion: A service-based, containerized design lets one toolkit standardize adversarial stress-testing of diverse LiDAR perception models before real-world deployment.

title: Open-set multi-view seahorse re-identification from underwater photograph sequences
summary: Automated animal re-identification from photograph sequences can facilitate minimally invasive Capture-Mark-Recapture studies at scale. Yet, photographs taken during an observation session can vary greatly in quality, not always providing the necessary information for accurate re-identification. In this paper, we present new methods for taxonomic classification, sex determination, and open-set re-identification from image sequences. We train and evaluate our models on a dataset of 35,914 photographs of 474 individual seahorses observed in the wild. We demonstrate that our approach, by combining information from multiple photographs, yields state-of-the-art performance.

AI.tldr: The paper presents methods for taxonomic classification, sex determination and open-set re-identification of seahorses from underwater photograph sequences. Combining information from multiple photographs yields state-of-the-art performance on a dataset of 35,914 photographs of 474 individual seahorses.
AI.motivation: Automated re-identification from photographs could enable minimally invasive Capture-Mark-Recapture studies at scale, but photo quality varies greatly within an observation session, so single photographs may not carry the information needed for accurate re-identification.
AI.method: Models for taxonomic classification, sex determination and open-set re-identification are trained and evaluated on image sequences, combining evidence across the multiple photographs of each animal.
AI.result: Combining information from multiple photographs yields state-of-the-art performance on a dataset of 35,914 photographs of 474 individual seahorses observed in the wild. The abstract gives no per-task figures.
AI.conclusion: Aggregating evidence across photograph sequences is an effective way to handle variable image quality in open-set seahorse re-identification for field studies.

authors: Udaya Sampath K. Perera Miriya Thanthrige
title: M-PFT: Angular Margin for Calibrated Prompt-Tuning of Fine-Tuned Vision-Language Models
summary: Prompt-tuning has emerged as a parameter-efficient technique for adapting large-scale vision-language models (VLMs) to downstream tasks while keeping the pre-trained weights frozen. However, prompt-tuned VLMs often suffer from a base-to-novel dual miscalibration problem, where models typically show underconfidence on base classes and overconfidence on novel classes. Current VLM calibration approaches address this dual miscalibration either separately or jointly, but lack a geometric understanding of the hyperspherical embedding space and thus fail to exploit angular discriminative properties to adjust distorted decision boundaries. To address this, we propose M-PFT, a novel angular-margin approach for prompt tuning that introduces two complementary objectives to promote class discriminability and semantic anchoring. This enlarges the angular margin by 1) minimizing the maximum cosine similarity between tunable class embeddings to reduce embedding collapse and 2) minimizing the angular distance between each tunable embedding and its corresponding zero-shot embedding to preserve semantic geometry. Extensive experiments across 9 prompt-tuning methods with various backbones on 15 diverse datasets show that our approach reduces the average calibration error on novel classes, while remaining competitive on base classes and maintaining comparable accuracy. Further analyses reveal that M-PFT effectively adjusts distorted decision boundaries induced by prompt tuning while preserving the pre-trained embedding space, improving calibration with negligible computational overhead.

AI.tldr: M-PFT is an angular-margin prompt-tuning method that reduces the calibration error on novel classes of prompt-tuned vision-language models while keeping base-class accuracy comparable. It uses two objectives that act on the hyperspherical embedding geometry.
AI.motivation: Prompt-tuned VLMs suffer base-to-novel dual miscalibration, being underconfident on base classes and overconfident on novel ones, and existing calibration approaches lack a geometric understanding of the hyperspherical embedding space.
AI.method: Two complementary objectives enlarge the angular margin: minimizing the maximum cosine similarity between tunable class embeddings to reduce embedding collapse, and minimizing the angular distance between each tunable embedding and its zero-shot embedding to preserve semantic geometry.
AI.result: Across 9 prompt-tuning methods, various backbones and 15 diverse datasets, M-PFT reduces the average calibration error on novel classes while remaining competitive on base classes and maintaining comparable accuracy, with negligible computational overhead.
AI.conclusion: Angular-margin regularization adjusts the distorted decision boundaries induced by prompt tuning while preserving the pre-trained embedding space, improving calibration at little cost.

title: Parametric Gaussian Noise Mixer (PGNM): Unified Synthesis of Camera Noise and Film Grain
comment: Technical report. 49 pages: 9-page main paper and 40-page supplementary material; 29 figures, 33 tables
summary: Noise synthesis is commonly approached through physical models of image formation or neural networks trained to generate noisy images. We explore a middle ground: an explicit statistical model fitted directly from paired clean and noisy images. A normalized convolution correlates a Gaussian field across pixels and color channels, and a lookup maps each Gaussian value to a residual given the clean intensity. Because the field stays standard Gaussian, the two components are fitted separately, without reproducing the physical process or training a neural generator. With one formulation for camera noise from SIDD and simulated film grain from Newson, the model has the lowest average distribution and correlation errors on SIDD among the evaluated methods and remains competitive on film grain. A denoiser trained on its noise comes closest to one trained on real noise, and a 1080p frame renders in 10 ms on GPU.

AI.tldr: PGNM is an explicit statistical noise model fitted from paired clean and noisy images that unifies camera noise and film grain synthesis. It has the lowest average distribution and correlation errors on SIDD among the evaluated methods and renders a 1080p frame in 10 ms on GPU.
AI.motivation: Noise synthesis is usually approached through physical image formation models or neural generators, and the paper seeks a middle ground that neither reproduces the physical process nor trains a neural generator.
AI.method: A normalized convolution correlates a Gaussian field across pixels and color channels, and a lookup maps each Gaussian value to a residual given the clean intensity. Because the field stays standard Gaussian, the two components are fitted separately.
AI.result: On camera noise from SIDD, the model has the lowest average distribution and correlation errors among the evaluated methods and remains competitive on simulated film grain from Newson. A denoiser trained on its noise comes closest to one trained on real noise, and a 1080p frame renders in 10 ms on GPU.
AI.conclusion: A simple, separately fitted statistical model can cover both camera noise and film grain, giving accurate and fast noise synthesis that is useful for training denoisers.

title: What Survives Label Downsampling? Exact Region Survival for Coarse Segmentation Targets
summary: Segmentation networks that predict at an output stride are trained against label maps downsampled by strided sampling, nearest-neighbor resampling or majority pooling. These methods label each coarse grid cell on its own, so a region that wins no cell is absent from the target and receives no positive label. We present MatchDown, which builds the coarse target from a minimum-cost matching between regions and the grid cells they occupy. It keeps as many regions as any one-region-per-cell target can, certifies how many losses are unavoidable, and with priority tiers (MatchDown-P) keeps every evaluated region (a region that a metric scores) of at least one cell's area. On COCO, Cityscapes and BBBC038 at factors 2 to 16, MatchDown-P loses exactly the minimum number of regions, whereas the downsampling used by StarDist, nnU-Net and connectomics pyramids loses four to five times as many on COCO at factor 8. Keeping a region in the target and reconstructing its shape are different problems: we show that no region lost by majority pooling can be reconstructed above IoU 0.5 by upsampling any coarse target, yet on BBBC038 a star-convex head trained on MatchDown targets segments 35% of the nuclei that majority pooling loses above IoU 0.5, against 15% when trained on majority targets and 24% on StarDist's strided target. On two nucleus datasets, with thresholds cross-validated for count error, this head has instance accuracy at IoU 0.5 (Acc50) 2.6 to 4.2 points above the strided target and at most 2.8 points below cell-center sampling, and a lower count error than the strided and cell-center targets on BBBC039. On BBBC039, an affinity head, which outputs one label per cell, lowers count error relative to majority targets by 9.3 nuclei per image at 7.2 points lower Acc50. MatchDown runs once, before training, in place of the label-downsampling step.

AI.tldr: MatchDown builds coarse segmentation targets by minimum-cost matching between regions and the grid cells they occupy, so far fewer regions are lost when labels are downsampled. MatchDown-P loses exactly the minimum number of regions on COCO, Cityscapes and BBBC038 across factors 2 to 16.
AI.motivation: Standard label downsampling (strided sampling, nearest-neighbor resampling and majority pooling) labels each coarse cell on its own, so a region that wins no cell is absent from the target and receives no positive label.
AI.method: The coarse target is built from a minimum-cost matching between regions and the cells they occupy. It keeps as many regions as any one-region-per-cell target can, certifies unavoidable losses, and with priority tiers (MatchDown-P) keeps every evaluated region of at least one cell's area. It runs once before training in place of the label-downsampling step.
AI.result: MatchDown-P loses exactly the minimum number of regions on COCO, Cityscapes and BBBC038 at factors 2 to 16, whereas the downsampling used by StarDist, nnU-Net and connectomics pyramids loses four to five times as many on COCO at factor 8. On BBBC038, a star-convex head trained on MatchDown targets segments 35% of the nuclei that majority pooling loses above IoU 0.5, against 15% for majority targets and 24% for StarDist's strided target. On two nucleus datasets the head's Acc50 is 2.6 to 4.2 points above the strided target, and an affinity head on BBBC039 lowers count error by 9.3 nuclei per image at 7.2 points lower Acc50.
AI.conclusion: Matching-based target construction keeps regions present in coarse targets and improves the reconstruction of nuclei that majority pooling loses, while fitting into existing segmentation pipelines as a pre-training step.

title: TokenRepel: Generating Diverse Image Sets Without Compromising Quality
summary: We present an inference-time approach that enhances the visual diversity of image sets generated by text-to-image models, without compromising the average image quality. Our method leverages the intrinsic geometry of hidden representations in pretrained models to diversify images generated from the same prompt. First, we introduce a token repulsion mechanism that increases the angle between feature tokens across samples. It takes a negative Riemannian gradient step on a von Mises-Fisher mixture distribution of tokens on the unit hypersphere. Second, to preserve the quality of each output image, we propose a token density preservation mechanism that projects the repulsion-induced prediction change onto a half-space aligned with the model's score direction. This encourages the updates to remain within the high-density regions learned by the generative model. We further extend this mechanism to the output of each intermediate layer, enabling finer-grained iterative guidance. We evaluate our method on three types of pretrained text-to-image models. Experiments show substantial gains in visual diversity under identical prompts, while maintaining a comparable level of image fidelity.

AI.tldr: TokenRepel is an inference-time method that increases the visual diversity of image sets generated from the same prompt by text-to-image models, without compromising average image quality. Experiments on three types of pretrained models show substantial diversity gains with comparable fidelity.
AI.motivation: Images generated from one prompt tend to be visually similar, and naive diversification can compromise the quality of the average image.
AI.method: A token repulsion mechanism increases the angle between feature tokens across samples by taking a negative Riemannian gradient step on a von Mises-Fisher mixture of tokens on the unit hypersphere. A token density preservation mechanism projects the repulsion-induced prediction change onto a half-space aligned with the model's score direction, keeping updates in high-density regions, and the mechanism is extended to the output of each intermediate layer.
AI.result: Experiments on three types of pretrained text-to-image models show substantial gains in visual diversity under identical prompts while maintaining a comparable level of image fidelity.
AI.conclusion: Geometry-aware repulsion constrained by the score direction offers an inference-time way to diversify generated image sets without sacrificing per-image quality.

title: PhysAg3D: Bridging 3D Generative and Agentic Models for High-Fidelity and Physically-Interactive Assets
summary: Generating interactive 3D assets from a single image requires realistic appearance, fidelity to the depicted object, and plausible physical behavior. Yet detailed geometry alone does not determine how an object should move or deform. We introduce PhysAg3D, which couples 3D generative models with agentic reasoning and tool use. A vision-language agent first infers semantic parts, candidate interactions, and physical priors from the image; a 3D generator then produces a textured whole-object mesh from the same image. A hierarchical interaction representation links these revisable priors to mechanisms and the generated surfaces they control, organizing interaction construction and refinement. Guided by this representation and observations of the mesh, the agent uses geometric and physical tools to construct parts, joints, deformable regions, and surface bindings while retaining useful generated geometry and materials. Rendered interactions and execution measurements guide targeted revisions within a fixed budget. The framework accommodates both rigid articulation and compliant deformation. Quantitative and qualitative evaluations on real photographs and external benchmarks demonstrate detailed, image-aligned assets with plausible interactions. Ablations support bounded refinement and source-surface preservation. Project Page: this http URL.

AI.tldr: PhysAg3D generates interactive 3D assets from a single image by coupling a 3D generative model with a vision-language agent that infers parts, candidate interactions and physical priors, then builds joints, deformable regions and surface bindings with geometric and physical tools. It accommodates both rigid articulation and compliant deformation.
AI.motivation: Detailed geometry alone does not determine how an object should move or deform, so interactive 3D assets need physically plausible behavior beyond appearance and shape.
AI.method: A vision-language agent infers semantic parts, candidate interactions and physical priors from the image, while a 3D generator produces a textured whole-object mesh from the same image. A hierarchical interaction representation links revisable priors to mechanisms and the generated surfaces they control. Guided by it and by mesh observations, the agent constructs parts, joints, deformable regions and surface bindings, then revises them within a fixed budget using rendered interactions and execution measurements.
AI.result: Quantitative and qualitative evaluations on real photographs and external benchmarks show detailed, image-aligned assets with plausible interactions. Ablations support bounded refinement and source-surface preservation. The abstract gives no numeric scores.
AI.conclusion: Combining generative geometry with agentic reasoning and physical tools can produce image-faithful, physically interactive 3D assets from a single image.

title: Spectral Invariant Fusion and Refinement for Domain Generalized Semantic Segmentation
summary: Domain generalized semantic segmentation is challenging because it requires accurate dense prediction on unseen domains without any access to target-domain data during training. Existing methods improve transferability through data diversification, invariant learning, or direct use of foundation models, but they often struggle to simultaneously suppress domain-sensitive interference and preserve fine-grained spatial cues. In this work, we propose SIFR, a frequency-aware dual-stream framework that tackles domain shift at both the fusion and decoding stages. SIFR uses spectral modeling as a unified principle to regulate both heterogeneous prior interaction and dense decoder refinement. Instead of directly fusing frozen CLIP and DINOv2 features, SIFR performs spectral-guided invariant fusion to filter out domain-sensitive responses while preserving complementary semantic and structural information. In addition, SIFR incorporates a spectral decoder refinement module that stabilizes multi-scale decoder features through low-frequency statistics-based normalization and adaptive frequency selection, thereby reducing the propagation of residual domain bias in dense prediction. This design enables SIFR to jointly improve domain robustness and segmentation precision under severe distribution shifts. Extensive experiments on multiple DGSS benchmarks, including synthetic-to-real, real-to-real, and adverse-weather settings, demonstrate consistent improvements over previous state-of-the-art methods.

AI.tldr: SIFR is a frequency-aware dual-stream framework for domain generalized semantic segmentation that fuses frozen CLIP and DINOv2 features through spectral-guided invariant fusion and refines decoder features with spectral modeling. It reports consistent improvements over previous state-of-the-art methods on multiple DGSS benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Domain generalized semantic segmentation requires accurate dense prediction on unseen domains without target data, yet existing methods struggle to suppress domain-sensitive interference while preserving fine-grained spatial cues.
AI.method: Rather than directly fusing frozen CLIP and DINOv2 features, spectral-guided invariant fusion filters out domain-sensitive responses while keeping complementary semantic and structural information. A spectral decoder refinement module stabilizes multi-scale decoder features through low-frequency statistics-based normalization and adaptive frequency selection.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on multiple DGSS benchmarks, including synthetic-to-real, real-to-real and adverse-weather settings, show consistent improvements over previous state-of-the-art methods. The abstract gives no numeric scores.
AI.conclusion: Spectral modeling applied to both feature fusion and decoding can jointly improve domain robustness and segmentation precision under severe distribution shifts.

title: MLLM-GS: Multimodal Large Language Model Prior-Guided Fast Novel View Synthesis in Extreme Environments
summary: Novel view synthesis (NVS) in degraded scenes aims to reconstruct 3D scenes from multi-view observations affected by various degradations, and to generate clear and photorealistic images at unseen viewpoints. Despite recent advances, existing methods often rely on degradation-specific models, limiting their generalization across diverse extreme environments. Generative models provide rich visual priors, but their outputs often suffer from pixel misalignment and color deviations, which can propagate into the reconstructed 3D scene and compromise reconstruction quality. Furthermore, the high computational and memory costs of 3D reconstruction hinder the practical application of NVS in extreme environments. To this end, we propose MLLM-GS, a multimodal large language model (MLLM) prior-guided framework for fast NVS in extreme environments. MLLM-GS consists of two branches: MLLM prior-guided view enhancement and fast 3D scene reconstruction. The former leverages the rich visual priors of a frozen MLLM to enhance views under different severe degradations and introduces a lightweight correction network to reduce pixel shifts and color distortions in MLLM outputs. With supervision from only a few paired clean views, this branch produces reliable enhanced views for all degraded observations, providing pseudo-GT views for subsequent 3D reconstruction. The latter improves 3DGS efficiency by optimizing rasterization, Gaussian memory layout, and parameter updates, reducing redundant computation, memory-access overhead, and optimization costs. Extensive experiments on multiple degraded scenes demonstrate that MLLM-GS effectively handles various severe degradations and achieves high-quality NVS with significantly lower reconstruction time and memory consumption. Project Page: this https URL

AI.tldr: MLLM-GS is a framework for fast novel view synthesis in degraded scenes that uses a frozen multimodal large language model as a visual prior to enhance views, followed by an efficiency-optimized 3DGS reconstruction. It aims for high-quality rendering with lower reconstruction time and memory consumption.
AI.motivation: Existing degraded-scene methods rely on degradation-specific models, generative priors suffer pixel misalignment and color deviations that propagate into the reconstruction, and 3D reconstruction is computationally expensive.
AI.method: The view enhancement branch uses a frozen MLLM's visual priors to enhance views under different degradations, with a lightweight correction network that reduces pixel shifts and color distortions in the MLLM outputs. Supervised by only a few paired clean views, it produces pseudo-ground-truth views. The reconstruction branch improves 3DGS efficiency by optimizing rasterization, Gaussian memory layout and parameter updates.
AI.result: Experiments on multiple degraded scenes show that MLLM-GS handles various severe degradations and achieves high-quality NVS with significantly lower reconstruction time and memory consumption. The abstract gives no numeric scores.
AI.conclusion: Correcting MLLM priors to supply pseudo-ground-truth views, combined with efficiency-oriented 3DGS optimization, makes novel view synthesis practical in extreme environments.

title: BiHashFormer: Hash-Driven Dual-Branch Transformer for Efficient Object Detection in HRW Shots
comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 34 pages including supplementary material and the NeurIPS checklist. Code: this https URL
summary: Recent advances in gigapixel-level imaging have brought High-Resolution Wide shots to the forefront of research. However, these images present significant challenges: extreme sparsity of foreground, gigapixel-level resolutions and interleaving of foreground and background. This causes traditional detectors and attention mechanisms to be hindered by background, resulting in inefficiency and inaccuracy. To tackle this problem, we propose BiHashFormer, a dual sparsified branch transformer built on hashing. RoI Selector will predict the foreground proportion for top-k selecting target-containing windows. The compression branch processes windows selected and refines attention into HashAttention by discarding half of the key-value pairs, reducing cost and improving efficiency. The compensation branch uses HashMiner to perform low-cost hash searches in the remaining regions, recovering features of missed objects. Experiments confirm that the selection relationship in HashAttention is one-way and reveal the preference of different queries for keys. In experiments on the gigapixel benchmark PANDA, BiHashFormer reduces 37.5% backbone FLOPs while improving AP50 to 81.0%. Moreover, this parallel dual-branch structure allows the model to avoid inference delays caused by inter-branch dependencies, while achieving much greater stability than single-branch models, specially with low rates of RoI selection.

AI.tldr: BiHashFormer is a dual-branch transformer for object detection in gigapixel High-Resolution Wide shots that uses hashing to skip background. On the PANDA benchmark it reduces backbone FLOPs by 37.5% while improving AP50 to 81.0%.
AI.motivation: HRW images have extreme foreground sparsity, gigapixel resolution and interleaved foreground and background, so traditional detectors and attention mechanisms are hindered by background, causing inefficiency and inaccuracy.
AI.method: An RoI Selector predicts the foreground proportion to select top-k target-containing windows. A compression branch applies HashAttention, which discards half of the key-value pairs in the selected windows. A compensation branch uses HashMiner to run low-cost hash searches in the remaining regions to recover features of missed objects. The two branches run in parallel.
AI.result: On the PANDA gigapixel benchmark, BiHashFormer reduces backbone FLOPs by 37.5% while improving AP50 to 81.0%. The parallel structure avoids inference delays from inter-branch dependencies and gives much greater stability than single-branch models, especially at low RoI selection rates.
AI.conclusion: Hash-based sparse attention combined with a parallel compensation branch offers an efficient and stable route to detection in gigapixel wide-field imagery.

title: ElasticFormer: Detecting Objects in HRW Shots via Elastic Computing Vision Transformer
comment: Published at CVPR 2026. 14 pages including supplementary material. Code: this https URL
summary: Recent advances in gigapixel-level imaging have brought High-Resolution Wide shots to the forefront of research. However, these images present significant challenges: extreme sparsity of foreground, gigapixel-level resolutions and diverse target counts. This makes traditional close-up detectors inaccurate and slow as they are overwhelmed by the background. Although previous research has explored sparse backbones, their fixed sparsity patterns lack the adaptability required to handle diverse target numbers. To address this, we introduce ElasticFormer, a sparse backbone that dynamically allocates computational resources based on foreground proportion. After scoring windows based on variance, proposed ElasticSelector module will predict the foreground proportion for top-k selection. The mechanism guides the model to select target-containing windows, scaling resources in areas where objects are clustered. We introduce a novel loss function combined with the 3-phase training strategy for ElasticSelector, allowing it to function properly when bounding box annotations are missing. A WSOD study is carried on PASCAL VOC 2007 to evaluate its extensibility. Further, ElasticNet is created to verify its backbone-agnostic nature. In experiments on the PANDA gigapixel benchmark, ElasticFormer reduces backbone FLOPs by 80% while achieving a significant improvement in AP50 when compared to fixed-ratio sparse methods.

AI.tldr: ElasticFormer is a sparse backbone for detecting objects in HRW shots that dynamically allocates computation according to foreground proportion. On the PANDA benchmark it reduces backbone FLOPs by 80% while achieving a significant AP50 improvement over fixed-ratio sparse methods.
AI.motivation: Close-up detectors become inaccurate and slow on HRW shots because the background overwhelms them, and previous sparse backbones use fixed sparsity patterns that cannot adapt to diverse target counts.
AI.method: Windows are scored by variance, and the ElasticSelector module predicts the foreground proportion for top-k selection, so resources scale with object clustering. A novel loss and a 3-phase training strategy let the selector function when bounding box annotations are missing. A weakly supervised detection study on PASCAL VOC 2007 tests extensibility, and ElasticNet is built to verify backbone-agnostic behavior.
AI.result: On the PANDA gigapixel benchmark, ElasticFormer reduces backbone FLOPs by 80% while achieving a significant AP50 improvement compared with fixed-ratio sparse methods. The abstract gives no further numbers.
AI.conclusion: Adaptive, foreground-proportion-driven sparsity is more effective than fixed patterns for HRW detection, and the selector design is backbone-agnostic.

title: UniRA: Unified Representation Alignment and Auto-Encoding for Efficient Diffusion Generation
summary: Diffusion transformers (DiTs) have become the dominant architecture for high-fidelity image synthesis, yet they suffer from slow training convergence and high computational cost. Two recent lines of work address this from complementary angles: Representation Alignment (REPA) accelerates DiT training by aligning intermediate features with a pretrained external representation model (e.g., DINOv2), while Representation Auto-Encoders (RAE) replace the pixel-space VAE with a compact representation-space tokenizer learned from self-supervised features. However, these approaches are developed and applied in isolation: REPA still relies on a pixel-space VAE for latent diffusion, and RAE does not exploit the alignment signal that accelerates the diffusion backbone. We present \textbf{UniRA}, a unified framework that couples representation alignment and representation auto-encoding into a single objective. UniRA learns a representation-space tokenizer whose output serves simultaneously as the diffusion target and the alignment anchor, so the tokenizer, the diffusion backbone, and the external representation model are co-optimized. We give a theoretical result showing that this joint optimization preserves the representation quality of the external model while accelerating diffusion convergence, and we derive a principled weighting that balances the reconstruction, alignment, and generation objectives. On ImageNet class-conditional generation at 256*256 and 512*512, UniRA matches or surpasses state-of-the-art DiTs (SD3, REPA, RAE) in FID while reducing training steps by up to 5*. We further show that the unified representation space supports improved zero-shot classification and linear probing, confirming that generation and understanding benefit from a shared, aligned latent space.

AI.tldr: UniRA couples representation alignment (REPA) and representation auto-encoding (RAE) into a single objective, so that a representation-space tokenizer serves as both the diffusion target and the alignment anchor. It matches or surpasses SD3, REPA and RAE in FID on ImageNet while reducing training steps by up to 5 times.
AI.motivation: REPA accelerates DiT training but still relies on a pixel-space VAE for latent diffusion, while RAE uses a representation-space tokenizer without exploiting the alignment signal, so the two lines of work are developed in isolation.
AI.method: A representation-space tokenizer learns an output that is simultaneously the diffusion target and the alignment anchor, so the tokenizer, the diffusion backbone and the external representation model are co-optimized. A theoretical result is given showing that this joint optimization preserves the external model's representation quality while accelerating diffusion convergence, and a principled weighting balances the reconstruction, alignment and generation objectives.
AI.result: On ImageNet class-conditional generation at 256*256 and 512*512, UniRA matches or surpasses state-of-the-art DiTs (SD3, REPA, RAE) in FID while reducing training steps by up to 5 times. The unified representation space also supports improved zero-shot classification and linear probing.
AI.conclusion: A shared, aligned latent space lets generation and understanding benefit together, with joint optimization accelerating diffusion convergence while preserving representation quality.

title: Mind The Gap (MTG-AD): Dataset and Fine-grained Evaluation for End-to-End Inline Audio Descriptions
comment: NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations & Datasets Track, camera ready
summary: Audio descriptions (AD) are essential for making visual media accessible to blind and low-vision (BLV) users. While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) offer a scalable solution for generating audio descriptions on-demand, their performance on ``inline'' audio descriptions -- which must fit within existing silences in a video -- remains under-explored, particularly for diverse user-generated content (UGC). We present a comprehensive investigation into MLLM-generated inline audio descriptions. First, we introduce MTG-AD, a professionally annotated dataset of 36 hours of videos, each averaging $\sim$5 mins. and 8k+ descriptions in total, co-created by paired blind and sighted AD professionals to provide a high-quality benchmark for this task. Second, we propose MTG-AD-Eval, an evaluation framework based on audio description expert guidelines that provides fine-grained, reference-free actionable metrics for model improvement. Crucially, our framework evaluates the end-to-end task: it renders the generated scripts into audio tracks to assess their fit within the original video's natural silences, minimizing disruptive overlaps. Our analysis across frontier MLLMs reveals that while models accurately describe visual events and substantially reduce speech overlaps, gaps persist in narrative pacing and flow. Finally, we empirically validate that our automated and reference-free metrics correlate significantly with human quality ratings from sighted raters and 7 BLV participants, finding that while users narrowly prefer human-authored audio descriptions, they find MLLM-generated audio descriptions highly beneficial for comprehension. We provide actionable system design guidance and release MTG-AD at this https URL and MTG-AD-Eval at this https URL.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces MTG-AD, a dataset of 36 hours of professionally co-created inline audio descriptions, and MTG-AD-Eval, a reference-free framework that renders generated descriptions into audio to test their fit within natural silences. Frontier MLLMs describe visual events accurately and substantially reduce speech overlaps but still lag in narrative pacing and flow.
AI.motivation: Inline audio descriptions must fit within existing silences in a video, and MLLM performance on this task, especially for diverse user-generated content, remains under-explored.
AI.method: MTG-AD contains videos averaging about 5 minutes each, with 8k+ descriptions co-created by paired blind and sighted audio description professionals. MTG-AD-Eval is based on audio description expert guidelines and provides fine-grained, reference-free actionable metrics, evaluating the end-to-end task by rendering generated scripts into audio tracks to assess their fit within the original video's natural silences.
AI.result: Analysis across frontier MLLMs shows accurate descriptions of visual events and substantially reduced speech overlaps, while gaps persist in narrative pacing and flow. The automated metrics correlate significantly with human quality ratings from sighted raters and 7 BLV participants. Users narrowly prefer human-authored audio descriptions but find MLLM-generated ones highly beneficial for comprehension.
AI.conclusion: The benchmark and reference-free metrics give actionable system design guidance for end-to-end inline audio description, with narrative pacing and flow as the main remaining gap.

title: DINOv2 for PET: A Pre-Training Domain Benchmark Across Classification, Segmentation, and Prognosis
summary: DINO (self-DIstillation with NO labels) has become a stan- dard for self-supervised pre-training, producing features that generalise across datasets and downstream tasks. In medical imaging it has been adopted mainly for radiology (X-ray, CT and MRI), where even natural- image DINO features transfer well. In the literature, these features have been reported to transfer worse to functional imaging such as PET. Yet PET-specific DINO models have barely been introduced, and even less validated across multiple tasks and datasets. We present PET-DINOv2-2D, the first DINOv2 model pre-trained on 2D PET, and benchmark it against open-source encoders: the origi- nal DINOv2 (pre-trained on the LVD-142M natural-image dataset) and OmniRad (pre-trained on CT, MRI and ultrasound). Using the same lightweight heads for every backbone, and despite far less pre-training data, PET-DINOv2-2D matches or outperforms both on three down- stream PET tasks: normal/abnormal classification, lesion segmentation and recurrence-free survival prognosis. Its advantage is largest when few labels are available, suggesting that PET pre-training gives more transferable, label-efficient features. Code is made available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: PET-DINOv2-2D is a DINOv2 model pre-trained on 2D PET images, benchmarked against the original DINOv2 and OmniRad encoders on three PET tasks. Despite far less pre-training data, it matches or outperforms both, with the largest advantage when few labels are available.
AI.motivation: DINO features from natural images and radiology are reported to transfer worse to functional imaging such as PET, and PET-specific DINO models have barely been introduced or validated across multiple tasks and datasets.
AI.method: The model is pre-trained on 2D PET and compared against DINOv2 (pre-trained on the LVD-142M natural-image dataset) and OmniRad (pre-trained on CT, MRI and ultrasound), using the same lightweight heads for every backbone.
AI.result: On normal/abnormal classification, lesion segmentation and recurrence-free survival prognosis, PET-DINOv2-2D matches or outperforms both baselines. Its advantage is largest when few labels are available.
AI.conclusion: PET pre-training yields more transferable and label-efficient features for PET analysis than general-purpose or other-modality pre-training.

title: Segment Anything Model Based Context Guided Mamba Unet for Medical Image Segmentation
summary: Medical image segmentation is crucial for clinical diagnosis and treatment planning, requiring both global contextual understanding and fine-grained structural precision. While the Segment Anything Model (SAM) demonstrates strong generalization capabilities, its direct application to medical images often lacks domain-specific adaptability. Meanwhile, State Space Models (SSMs)-based methods, such as Mamba, efficiently capture long-range dependencies but may struggle with preserving fine anatomical details. To address these challenges, we propose a segment anything model based context guided mamba unet, SAMBA-UNet, a novel framework that integrates SAM's context knowledge with Mamba's hierarchical feature learning to enhance both global representation and local detail refinement. Specifically, we introduce the Hierarchical Context Enhancement Module (HCEM), an attention-based fusion module that deeply incorporates the multi-level features of SAM and Mamba to improve detail perception and segmentation precision. Additionally, we employ LoRA and Adapter-based fine-tuning to adapt SAM to medical imaging tasks, further enhancing its domain-specific segmentation capability and robustness. We conducted a comprehensive study on several medical segmentation datasets, including Synapse, ISIC17, and ISIC18, evaluating our method across multiple metrics. Experimental results demonstrate that SAMBA-UNet achieves state-of-the-art performance, effectively balancing generalization, segmentation accuracy, and computational efficiency. Our code will be released upon acceptance.

AI.tldr: SAMBA-UNet integrates SAM's context knowledge with Mamba's hierarchical feature learning through a Hierarchical Context Enhancement Module for medical image segmentation. It reports state-of-the-art performance on Synapse, ISIC17 and ISIC18.
AI.motivation: Direct application of SAM to medical images often lacks domain-specific adaptability, while Mamba-based state space models capture long-range dependencies but may struggle to preserve fine anatomical details.
AI.method: The Hierarchical Context Enhancement Module is an attention-based fusion module that combines multi-level SAM and Mamba features to improve detail perception and segmentation precision. LoRA and Adapter-based fine-tuning adapt SAM to medical imaging tasks.
AI.result: Experiments on Synapse, ISIC17 and ISIC18 across multiple metrics show state-of-the-art performance, balancing generalization, segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. The abstract gives no numeric scores.
AI.conclusion: Fusing SAM's contextual knowledge with Mamba's hierarchical learning improves both global representation and local detail refinement for medical image segmentation.

title: EPC-RawDC: Equivariant Physics Constrained 3D Diffusion with Raw Data Consistency for CBCT to CT Image Synthesis
summary: Cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) is widely used for image guided and adaptive radiotherapy, but scatter, noise, reconstruction artifacts, and inaccurate Hounsfield units limit its quantitative use. Recent diffusion approaches for CBCT to CT synthesis remain largely image driven, with limited use of the underlying acquisition physics. We propose EPC-RawDC, a conditional 3D latent diffusion framework that combines volumetric generative modeling with two complementary constraints derived from the same scanner specific CBCT forward model. First, geometry equivariant projection constraint exploits the rotational equivariance of the CBCT forward operator by supervising the synthesized CT through correspondingly transformed reference projections. Second, raw data consistency uses noisy projection measurements of the individual acquisition as scan specific supervision during training. The framework was evaluated on two independent clinical cohorts with distinct scanner geometries and projection sources. For JUST, the physics constraints used measured clinical raw CBCT projections acquired with an Elekta system, whereas for SynthRAD2025 the projection data were simulated from the reference CT using a Varian geometry with Poisson photon statistics. EPC-RawDC achieved an SSIM of 0.97 in both cohorts and improved PSNR over DDPM by 2.66 dB on SynthRAD2025 and 2.10 dB on JUST, while reducing mean MAE by 20.3% and 19.0%, respectively. On SynthRAD2025, projection consistency and equivariant errors were reduced by 55.0% and 41.4% relative to DDPM. These results demonstrate that combining a volumetric diffusion prior with scanner geometry and scan specific projection measurements improves quantitative CBCT to CT synthesis across both simulated and measured projection domains. Code available after publication at this https URL.

AI.tldr: EPC-RawDC is a conditional 3D latent diffusion framework for CBCT-to-CT synthesis that adds two constraints derived from the scanner's forward model. It reaches an SSIM of 0.97 in both cohorts and improves PSNR over DDPM by 2.66 dB on SynthRAD2025 and 2.10 dB on JUST.
AI.motivation: Scatter, noise, reconstruction artifacts and inaccurate Hounsfield units limit the quantitative use of CBCT, and existing diffusion approaches for CBCT-to-CT synthesis are largely image-driven with limited use of the acquisition physics.
AI.method: Two constraints are derived from the scanner-specific CBCT forward model. A geometry-equivariant projection constraint exploits rotational equivariance by supervising the synthesized CT through correspondingly transformed reference projections. A raw data consistency term uses noisy projection measurements of each individual acquisition as scan-specific supervision during training.
AI.result: Evaluated on JUST (measured Elekta projections) and SynthRAD2025 (projections simulated from the reference CT with a Varian geometry and Poisson photon statistics), EPC-RawDC reaches SSIM 0.97 in both cohorts, improves PSNR over DDPM by 2.66 dB and 2.10 dB, and reduces mean MAE by 20.3% and 19.0%. On SynthRAD2025, projection consistency and equivariant errors fall by 55.0% and 41.4% relative to DDPM.
AI.conclusion: Combining a volumetric diffusion prior with scanner geometry and scan-specific projection measurements improves quantitative CBCT-to-CT synthesis across both simulated and measured projection domains.

title: Localizing Concepts in Visual Autoregressive Models
summary: Understanding the internal routing of visual concepts is crucial for the safe and controllable adaptation of generative models. While concept localization has been widely studied in diffusion models, the emerging paradigm of next-scale visual autoregressive models remains largely unexplored. In this paper, we introduce LoCo, the first model-agnostic framework to localize where and when specific concepts emerge within autoregressive models. Driven by the native coarse-to-fine nature of next-scale generation, our method precisely maps conceptual knowledge across three distinct dimensions: Layer, Scale, and Position. To systematically localize and evaluate concept routing without context bias, we propose LoCoBench, a comprehensive dataset spanning 10 diverse categories. Extensive probing on image and video autoregressive models like Infinity, HunyuanImage-3.0, and InfinityStar shows that the localized positions are both interpretable and causally related to concept emergence. Building on these insights, we apply our localization method to three key applications: concept erasure, model personalization, and adversarial concept injection. Experiments demonstrate that our targeted intervention achieves state-of-the-art performance, substantially reducing computational overhead while preserving benign utility. Overall, our findings offer insights into how conceptual knowledge is routed during autoregressive generation, introducing a practical pathway for more interpretable, efficient, and secure adaptation.

AI.tldr: LoCo is a model-agnostic framework that localizes where and when specific concepts emerge in next-scale visual autoregressive models, mapping them along layer, scale and position. Its localized positions are interpretable and causally related to concept emergence, and they support concept erasure, model personalization and adversarial concept injection.
AI.motivation: Concept localization is well studied in diffusion models, but the emerging next-scale visual autoregressive paradigm remains largely unexplored, although knowing how concepts are routed is needed for safe and controllable adaptation.
AI.method: LoCo maps conceptual knowledge across Layer, Scale and Position, exploiting the native coarse-to-fine nature of next-scale generation. To localize and evaluate concept routing without context bias, the authors propose LoCoBench, a dataset spanning 10 diverse categories.
AI.result: Probing image and video autoregressive models including Infinity, HunyuanImage-3.0 and InfinityStar shows that localized positions are interpretable and causally related to concept emergence. Applied to concept erasure, model personalization and adversarial concept injection, the targeted intervention achieves state-of-the-art performance while substantially reducing computational overhead and preserving benign utility.
AI.conclusion: The findings reveal how conceptual knowledge is routed during autoregressive generation and offer a practical path to more interpretable, efficient and secure adaptation of these models.

title: BRACHIO: Broad Representations Across Centres for Head-and-neck Imaging Oncology (HECKTOR 2026)
comment: HECKTOR Challenge 2026, MICCAI, head and neck cancer, PET imaging
summary: The HECKTOR 2026 challenge benchmarks machine learning for head and neck cancer, where teams delineate primary and nodal tumour volumes, perform TN staging, and predict recurrence-free survival (RFS). This report describes the submissions for the HECKTOR challenge of team nucli. As the three tasks span both dense and global information from multicentric PET/CT scans, we utilise self-supervised pre-trained encoders, training a 2D DINOv2 encoder (PET-DINOv2-MIPs) on HECKTOR 2026's PET scans. Our final test submission ensembles a DynUNet trained from scratch with a SwinUNETR whose Swin trunk was initialised from a SimMIM-pre-trained checkpoint for segmentation, reaching a mean Dice of 0.5409. For TN staging, GTVp/GTVn geometric features from the segmentation masks are fit to stage probabilities by logistic regression (LR) and fused with PET-DINOv2-MIPs deep features (PCA + LR) via a second-level LR, reaching balanced accuracies of 0.3962 (T-stage) and 0.6432 (N-stage). For the RFS prognosis task, we fine-tune the last two blocks of the PET-DINOv2-MIPs ViT-S encoder jointly with an MLP head under a CoxPH loss, concatenating clinical covariates with the imaging features, reaching a test Harrell's C-index of 0.6577 and a weighted challenge score of 0.5802. The prognosis result is comparable to the best entry of the previous edition and consistent with our internal cross-validation, while our segmentation result is well below it and limits the staging results that depend on it.

AI.tldr: The HECKTOR 2026 challenge report from team nucli covers tumour segmentation, TN staging and recurrence-free survival prediction on PET/CT, using self-supervised DINOv2 encoders and ensembles. The segmentation result is well below the best previous entry, which limits the staging results that depend on it, while the prognosis result is comparable to the best entry of the previous edition.
AI.motivation: The three HECKTOR 2026 tasks span both dense and global information from multicentric PET/CT scans, so the approach needs pre-trained encoders and features that serve all three tasks.
AI.method: A 2D DINOv2 encoder (PET-DINOv2-MIPs) is trained on HECKTOR 2026 PET scans. Segmentation ensembles a DynUNet trained from scratch with a SwinUNETR whose Swin trunk is initialised from a SimMIM-pre-trained checkpoint. TN staging fits logistic regression on GTVp/GTVn geometric features from the masks and fuses it with PCA plus logistic regression on deep features through a second-level logistic regression. RFS prognosis fine-tunes the last two blocks of the ViT-S encoder jointly with an MLP head under a CoxPH loss, concatenating clinical covariates with the imaging features.
