AI.result: Test mean Dice of 0.5409 for segmentation; balanced accuracies of 0.3962 (T-stage) and 0.6432 (N-stage); test Harrell's C-index of 0.6577 and weighted challenge score of 0.5802 for RFS prognosis. The prognosis result is consistent with internal cross-validation.
AI.conclusion: Self-supervised PET encoders can support dense and global tasks in this challenge, but weak segmentation propagates into the staging results, so segmentation quality is the limiting factor for those tasks.

title: Uncertainty-aware Coarse-to-Fine Main Pancreatic Duct Segmentation for Width Measurement in 3D MRCP
summary: Assessment of the main pancreatic duct (MPD) from volumetric magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) scans is an essential task for ductal dilatation diagnosis and pancreatic cancer analysis. However, manual assessment is affected by reader variability in which automated analysis may assist. Nevertheless, fully automated and uncertainty-aware MPD analysis from volumetric MRCP remains underexplored area of research. In this study, we propose an automatic and uncertainty-aware deep learning-based pipeline for MPD segmentation and maximum-width analysis from MRCP scans. A coarse localisation model first identifies the ductal region-of-interest, followed by a fine model that segments the MPD within the region. The dataset consists of 256 MPD-segmented MRCP scans from 69 patients. A randomly selected holdout test subset of 14 patients with 55 MRCP volumes was used for evaluation. We employed a five-model cross-validation ensemble for improved performance and uncertainty estimation. The best MPD segmentation performance was 0.634 DSC, 0.744 precision, and 0.593 recall. The mean absolute error for maximum MPD width prediction was 0.355~mm and dilated MPD ($\geq 5$~mm) was detected with 75.0\% sensitivity and 74.4\% specificity. These novel results suggest that automated MPD segmentation can be used to aid MRCP-based duct measurements.

AI.tldr: An uncertainty-aware two-stage pipeline segments the main pancreatic duct in 3D MRCP and measures its maximum width. The best segmentation reaches 0.634 DSC, and the mean absolute error for maximum width is 0.355 mm.
AI.motivation: Manual assessment of the main pancreatic duct from MRCP is affected by reader variability, and fully automated, uncertainty-aware analysis of volumetric MRCP is described as underexplored.
AI.method: A coarse localisation model first identifies the ductal region of interest, and a fine model segments the duct within it. A five-model cross-validation ensemble is used for performance and uncertainty estimation. The dataset has 256 MPD-segmented scans from 69 patients, with a holdout test set of 14 patients (55 volumes).
AI.result: The best MPD segmentation reaches 0.634 DSC, 0.744 precision and 0.593 recall. The mean absolute error for maximum width is 0.355 mm, and dilated MPD (at least 5 mm) is detected with 75.0% sensitivity and 74.4% specificity.
AI.conclusion: The authors suggest that automated MPD segmentation can aid MRCP-based duct measurements.

title: Morphology-Aware Channel-Decoupled Mamba Network for Medical Image Segmentation
summary: Accurate multi-organ segmentation in computed tomography (CT) is essential for computer-aided diagnosis, treatment planning, and disease monitoring. However, substantial variations in organ shape and size, together with low tissue contrast and ambiguous boundaries, complicate the modeling of heterogeneous anatomical structures. To address these challenges, we propose a Morphology-Aware Channel-Decoupled Mamba Network (MCDNet), which integrates adaptive local structural enhancement with channel-decoupled long-range modeling. Specifically, we introduce a Morphology-Aware Channel-Decoupled State-Space (MCSS) block that divides feature channels into separate processing groups, allowing differentiated structural representations to be learned within an efficient state-space framework. Within each group, a Morphology-Aware Enhancement Module (MAEM) combines deformable convolutions with channel attention to adapt local feature extraction to anatomical shape variations. Group-wise state-space modeling then captures long-range spatial dependencies, and channel gating adaptively integrates the resulting features. Experiments on the Synapse abdominal CT dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of MCDNet, achieving an average Dice Similarity Coefficient of 81.61% for multi-organ segmentation.

AI.tldr: MCDNet is a Mamba-based network for multi-organ CT segmentation that combines deformable convolutions with channel-decoupled state-space modelling. It reaches an average Dice of 81.61% on the Synapse abdominal CT dataset.
AI.motivation: Multi-organ CT segmentation is difficult because organ shape and size vary widely, and low tissue contrast and ambiguous boundaries complicate modelling of heterogeneous anatomy.
AI.method: The MCSS block splits feature channels into separate groups for state-space processing. Within each group, the MAEM module combines deformable convolutions with channel attention to adapt local features to shape variation. Group-wise state-space modelling captures long-range dependencies, and channel gating integrates the resulting features.
AI.result: An average Dice Similarity Coefficient of 81.61% for multi-organ segmentation on the Synapse abdominal CT dataset. The abstract reports no baseline comparison.
AI.conclusion: The authors present channel-decoupled state-space modelling with morphology-aware local enhancement as an effective approach for multi-organ CT segmentation.

title: Neural Blind Deconvolution for Image Scanning Microscopy
summary: Image scanning microscopy (ISM) acquires one scanned image per detector element, which are then fused into a single image by multi-image deconvolution to obtain a super-resolved image. Its accuracy, however, depends on point spread function (PSF) models that sample- and system-induced aberrations often invalidate. Since differences between the scanned images encode aberration information, we propose a training-free blind Deep Image Prior (DIP) framework that jointly estimates the specimen and the detector-dependent PSFs. The PSFs are parametrised through the detector geometry and shared excitation and emission PSFs, reducing the unknowns while preserving the physical ISM model, and a Gaussian pre-initialisation stabilises the blind optimisation. On experimental tubulin data, blind DIP recovers finer filamentous structures than multi-image deconvolution and DIP with fixed theoretical PSFs, while adapting the PSFs to the measurements.

AI.tldr: A training-free blind Deep Image Prior framework for image scanning microscopy jointly estimates the specimen and the detector-dependent point spread functions. On experimental tubulin data it recovers finer filaments than multi-image deconvolution and DIP with fixed theoretical PSFs.
AI.motivation: ISM accuracy depends on PSF models that sample- and system-induced aberrations often invalidate, while differences between the scanned images carry information about those aberrations.
AI.method: The PSFs are parametrised through the detector geometry and shared excitation and emission PSFs, which reduces the number of unknowns while preserving the physical ISM model. A Gaussian pre-initialisation stabilises the blind optimisation.
AI.result: On experimental tubulin data, blind DIP recovers finer filamentous structures than multi-image deconvolution and than DIP with fixed theoretical PSFs, while adapting the PSFs to the measurements.
AI.conclusion: Joint blind estimation of the specimen and PSFs within a training-free DIP framework is presented as a way to handle unmodelled aberrations in ISM reconstruction.

title: RepConTUR: A Report-Conditioned Volumetric Multimodal Model for Abdominal Tumor Segmentation
summary: Tumor delineation is required for radiotherapy planning, yet automatic segmentation is limited by errors, predominantly false positives, that distort dose and increase editing time. The radiology report accompanies the scan and localizes disease at the suborgan level, but existing text-promptable models condition on short referring phrases, and most operate in 2D. We present RepConTUR, a single native-3D early-fusion multimodal model that conditions volumetric abdominal tumor segmentation on the narrative report. We extend AbdomenAtlas 3.0 to a suborgan-level promptable segmentation dataset and generate report-based VQA pairs, yielding four report-derived tasks on the same annotations: referring segmentation (RES), report-grounded segmentation (GSEG), report generation (RRG), and visual question answering (VQA). We train RepConTUR, comprising a 3D CT encoder, an early-fusion language model, and a native-3D segmentation module, jointly on the four tasks. Across liver, kidney and pancreas, RepConTUR attains the highest Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), instance-wise precision, and detection F1 among the text-promptable baselines, and adding the report raises mean precision while leaving recall comparable. Against two vision-only specialists, nnU-Net and the report-supervised R-Super, RepConTUR attains the highest value on every in-domain metric for liver and pancreas and the highest mean DSC, recall, precision, and detection F1 over the four out-of-distribution public cohorts. Ablations indicate that conditioning on the narrative report raises detection F1 from 0.499 to 0.528 within the same model, that joint GSEG training raises RES F1 from 0.450 to 0.482, and that the native-3D segmentation module raises GSEG F1 from 0.139 to 0.528 over its 2D counterpart. Code is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: RepConTUR is a native-3D early-fusion model that conditions volumetric abdominal tumour segmentation on the radiology report. It is trained jointly on four report-derived tasks and outperforms text-promptable baselines and vision-only specialists on several metrics.
AI.motivation: Automatic tumour segmentation makes errors, mostly false positives, that distort dose and increase editing time. Existing text-promptable models condition on short referring phrases rather than the full narrative report, and most operate in 2D.
AI.method: The model combines a 3D CT encoder, an early-fusion language model and a native-3D segmentation module, trained jointly on referring segmentation, report-grounded segmentation, report generation and visual question answering. The data is AbdomenAtlas 3.0 extended to a suborgan-level promptable segmentation dataset with report-based VQA pairs.
AI.result: Among text-promptable baselines, RepConTUR attains the highest DSC, instance-wise precision and detection F1 across liver, kidney and pancreas. Against nnU-Net and R-Super it attains the highest value on every in-domain metric for liver and pancreas, and the highest mean DSC, recall, precision and detection F1 over four out-of-distribution cohorts. Report conditioning raises detection F1 from 0.499 to 0.528, joint GSEG training raises RES F1 from 0.450 to 0.482, and the native-3D module raises GSEG F1 from 0.139 to 0.528 over its 2D counterpart.
AI.conclusion: Report conditioning, joint multi-task training and native 3D processing each improve tumour segmentation in the reported ablations, with the report raising precision while recall stays comparable.

title: SelfThinker: Self-Evolving Reasoning via Reliability-Verified Intrinsic Visual Thoughts
summary: Unified multimodal models can both generate and understand images within a single set of weights, offering an opportunity to use image synthesis as training supervision for visual comprehension. However, existing visual chain-of-thought methods rely on human-annotated helper images during training and require slow image generation at test time. We present SelfThinker, the first self-evolving framework that turns a unified model's self-generated visual thoughts into stronger understanding without human image annotations. Given a visual problem, SelfThinker samples candidate helper images from its generation pathway and uses its frozen understanding pathway to score each candidate via conditional pointwise mutual information. High-utility visual thoughts then refine the generator via flow matching and serve as privileged teacher context for on-policy self-distillation. At inference, SelfThinker reasons directly from the original image in text without generating intermediate images. Although trained only on small synthetic visual-search and navigation datasets, SelfThinker transfers broadly to natural-image and spatial benchmarks, raising the seven-benchmark average of ThinkMorph-7B from 52.7 to 64.0 (+11.3 points). Controlled image-perturbation probes further show that SelfThinker surpasses ThinkMorph-7B by up to 40.4 points and its pretrained BAGEL-7B backbone by up to 23.2 points across fine-grained and spatial perception tasks. Our code is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: SelfThinker is a self-evolving framework that uses a unified multimodal model's own generated visual thoughts, filtered by conditional pointwise mutual information, to improve visual understanding without human helper images. The seven-benchmark average of ThinkMorph-7B rises from 52.7 to 64.0.
AI.motivation: Existing visual chain-of-thought methods need human-annotated helper images during training and slow image generation at test time.
AI.method: The model samples candidate helper images from its generation pathway and scores each with its frozen understanding pathway via conditional pointwise mutual information. High-utility visual thoughts refine the generator through flow matching and serve as privileged teacher context for on-policy self-distillation. At inference it reasons from the original image in text, without generating intermediate images.
AI.result: Trained only on small synthetic visual-search and navigation datasets, it raises the seven-benchmark average of ThinkMorph-7B from 52.7 to 64.0 (+11.3 points). It surpasses ThinkMorph-7B by up to 40.4 points and its BAGEL-7B backbone by up to 23.2 points on fine-grained and spatial perception probes.
AI.conclusion: Self-generated visual thoughts, filtered for reliability, can supervise comprehension and transfer to natural-image and spatial benchmarks without human image annotation.

title: SynthFaces: Balanced Large Scale Human Dataset
comment: accepted at BMVC 2026 github: this https URL
summary: The pursuit of fair and equitable AI in human-centric tasks is critically hindered by the inherent biases and privacy risks of real-world datasets, which offer imbalanced representations of identity and often contain sensitive personal information. Consequently, state-of-the-art generative models trained on this skewed data exhibit unfair performance, particularly in identity-preserving generation. In this work we propose a pipeline for controllable generation of dataset with diverse faces for generative models training and finetuning. We achieve this by expanding foundational Arc2Face diffusion model with a flow matching generative model in the manifold of identity embeddings. We demonstrate that such approach achieves both goals of generative fidelity and label diversity not present in real human-centric datasets. As a result we collect and further contextualize a highly balanced identity-centric dataset of humans named SynthFaces. By design, our released images and identities are synthetic, reducing direct reliance on real personal images; we empirically check identity separation with a nearest-neighbor non-leakage metric. We purpose it for training and tuning of fair models for various downstream tasks, and showcase its usability in finetuning an existing adapter-based method for personalized generation.

AI.tldr: SynthFaces is a balanced, identity-centric synthetic human dataset produced by extending the Arc2Face diffusion model with a flow matching model in the identity-embedding manifold. The authors use it to finetune an adapter-based personalised generation method.
AI.motivation: Real human-centric datasets are imbalanced in identity representation and contain sensitive personal information, so generative models trained on them perform unfairly, especially in identity-preserving generation.
AI.method: The pipeline extends Arc2Face with a flow matching generative model operating on identity embeddings, to control the generation of diverse faces for training and finetuning. Identity separation is checked with a nearest-neighbour non-leakage metric.
AI.result: The approach is reported to achieve both generative fidelity and label diversity absent from real human-centric datasets, and the dataset is shown to be usable for finetuning an existing adapter-based personalised generation method. The abstract gives no numbers.
AI.conclusion: The dataset is intended for training and tuning fairer models on downstream tasks, and its synthetic identities reduce direct reliance on real personal images.

title: Learning a Motion Manifold to Constrain Ambiguity in Unsupervised 4D Medical Image Interpolation
summary: Unsupervised 4D medical image interpolation reconstructs intermediate anatomical states from temporally sparse observations without intermediate supervision. Distinct motion fields may attain comparable endpoint agreement while producing different intermediate anatomy, giving rise to motion ambiguity. This ambiguity is difficult to constrain when many independently adjustable motion variables must be estimated from the observed endpoints. We develop a framework that learns a motion manifold to restrict candidate motion fields while retaining sample-specific variation. Cross-Sample Spectral Basis Learning extracts recurring motion structure from endpoint-derived dense estimates and encodes it in a shared spectral basis. Sample-Conditioned Cayley Basis Reorientation uses predicted motion coordinates to rotate the effective motion directions for each endpoint pair without increasing the number of independent coordinates. Their composition defines a nonlinear family of complete velocity fields across endpoint pairs, accommodating anatomical and motion-state differences within a restricted representation. Integrating each predicted field supports bidirectional reconstruction at arbitrary intermediate times. Theoretical analysis establishes sufficient conditions under which endpoint observations distinguish nearby motions within the learned family. Experiments on ACDC and 4D-Lung demonstrate state-of-the-art performance among the evaluated methods trained without intermediate volumes and competitive results against methods using intermediate supervision.

AI.tldr: The paper learns a motion manifold for unsupervised 4D medical image interpolation, restricting candidate motion fields so that intermediate anatomy is better constrained. It reports state-of-the-art results among methods trained without intermediate volumes on ACDC and 4D-Lung.
AI.motivation: Distinct motion fields can match the observed endpoints while producing different intermediate anatomy, so motion ambiguity is hard to constrain when many independent motion variables are estimated from endpoints alone.
AI.method: Cross-Sample Spectral Basis Learning extracts recurring motion structure from endpoint-derived dense estimates into a shared spectral basis. Sample-Conditioned Cayley Basis Reorientation rotates the motion directions for each endpoint pair using predicted coordinates, without adding independent coordinates. Integrating the resulting velocity field supports bidirectional reconstruction at arbitrary intermediate times.
AI.result: On ACDC and 4D-Lung, the method achieves state-of-the-art performance among the evaluated methods trained without intermediate volumes, and competitive results against methods that use intermediate supervision. Theoretical analysis gives sufficient conditions under which endpoints distinguish nearby motions in the learned family.
AI.conclusion: A restricted, learned motion family can reduce ambiguity in unsupervised 4D interpolation while keeping sample-specific variation.

title: VideoMemBench: How Well Do MLLMs Remember in Video Conversations?
summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can now process hour-long videos, making extended multi-turn dialogue over a single video a natural mode of use. Sustaining such a dialogue requires more than answering each question in isolation: the model must retrieve and reuse information established earlier in the conversation, both what it has seen and what it has said, an ability we term in-context video memory. Existing video QA benchmarks leave this ability unmeasured: their questions are mutually independent, never reference one another, and each is answerable from the video alone, so nothing ever requires carrying information across turns. We introduce VideoMemBench, in which each sample pairs a single video with a long multi-turn dialogue, whose turns are connected by typed cross-turn dependencies: an Episodic Dependency refers back to a visual episode described in an earlier turn, probing memory of what the model has seen, while an Answer Dependency builds on the model's own earlier answer, probing memory of what the model has said. Every dependency is verified considering two properties: 1) necessity, meaning the question cannot be answered without its earlier turns, and 2) non-leakage, meaning the question does not restate the information from its earlier turns. To enforce these properties, we design a construction pipeline with three LLM roles: a planner, a generator, and a judger, with each dialogue reviewed by human experts. VideoMemBench comprises 326 videos with 2,476 turns, of which 1,387 depend on earlier turns, including multi-parent dependencies and long-range call-back. Among over 20 evaluated open- and closed-source MLLMs, Claude Opus 5 performs the best with an overall score of only 45.7\%, highlighting the challenge of in-context video memory. Our dataset and evaluation are released.

AI.tldr: VideoMemBench is a benchmark for in-context video memory in multi-turn dialogues over a single video, with cross-turn dependencies verified for necessity and non-leakage. Claude Opus 5 scores best among over 20 evaluated MLLMs, at 45.7% overall.
AI.motivation: Existing video QA benchmarks use mutually independent questions, so they never test whether a model carries information across turns, either what it has seen or what it has said.
AI.method: Each sample pairs one video with a long multi-turn dialogue whose turns are linked by typed dependencies: episodic dependencies refer back to visual episodes, and answer dependencies build on the model's own earlier answers. A construction pipeline with planner, generator and judger LLM roles is reviewed by human experts.
AI.result: The benchmark comprises 326 videos with 2,476 turns, of which 1,387 depend on earlier turns. Claude Opus 5 has the best overall score of 45.7% among over 20 open- and closed-source MLLMs evaluated.
AI.conclusion: In-context video memory is challenging for current MLLMs, and the dataset and evaluation are released.

title: NeurEO: dissecting Earth observation embeddings with computational neuroscience
comment: Originally published at the EurIPS 2025 REO workshop
summary: Earth embeddings are compressed representations of rich Earth observation data that enable downstream models to tackle a wide range of complex geospatial tasks. Yet, this increase in performance comes at the cost of decreased interpretability, as the semantic meaning of Earth embeddings is unknown. To address this challenge, we borrow methods from the field of computational neuroscience, which aim to interpret activity in (biological) neurons. Here, we adapt and apply these methods to assign meaning to AlphaEarth embeddings. We analyse embedding features both as stand-alone data, equivalent to spontaneous neural activity, and in relation to land cover and elevation correlates, equivalent to stimulus-response neural activity. We demonstrate correlational and multi-scale structure in the embedding features. Embedding features can display highly specific and directional tuning to land cover and elevation, such as a `North vs South woodland edge' response. When we remove the main trends of combined land cover responses (like water versus land tuning), we discover fine-grained representational details with increased effective dimensionality. Together, our analyses start to unravel what these Earth embeddings represent, which is critical for developing trustworthy downstream applications.

AI.tldr: NeurEO applies computational neuroscience methods to interpret AlphaEarth Earth embeddings, analysing features as if they were neurons with spontaneous and stimulus-response activity. It finds directional tuning to land cover and elevation, and finer structure once the main trends are removed.
AI.motivation: Earth embeddings enable strong geospatial performance but lose interpretability, since the semantic meaning of their features is unknown.
AI.method: Methods from computational neuroscience for interpreting neural activity are adapted to the embeddings. Features are analysed alone, analogous to spontaneous activity, and against land cover and elevation correlates, analogous to stimulus-response activity.
AI.result: The features show correlational and multi-scale structure and can display specific, directional tuning to land cover and elevation, such as a North vs South woodland edge response. After the main land cover trends are removed, finer representational details with higher effective dimensionality emerge.
AI.conclusion: The analyses begin to show what Earth embeddings represent, which the authors consider critical for trustworthy downstream applications.

title: Hierarchical Step Decomposition for Training-free Online Video Step Grounding
summary: Given a set of procedural steps, Video Step Grounding (VSG) aims to identify which steps occur in a video and localize when they are performed. Existing methods are either offline, requiring access to the full video before making predictions, or online, but relying on fixed-length video segments producing noisy, over-segmented outputs. In this work, we propose Hierarchical Step Decomposition (HSD), a training-free framework for online VSG that leverages the semantic understanding capabilities of Large Multimodal Models. HSD addresses two central challenges in online grounding: constructing semantically coherent temporal segments from a streaming video, and bridging the semantic gap between coarse procedural step descriptions and visual observations. To construct elementary temporal units, HSD incrementally groups incoming segments into semantically consistent events, using an anchor caption that is continuously validated against the visual stream. Based on these events, we perform zero-shot procedural step classification and selectively refine uncertain predictions by decomposing candidate steps into finegrained substeps that capture more nuanced visual evidence. By operating on semantically coherent events rather than every fixed-length segment, HSD reduces redundant computation and produces more stable predictions. Experiments on HT-Step, Ego4D Goal-Step, and CrossTask show that HSD substantially outperforms state-of-the-art methods, overall achieving better step recognition, more accurate temporal localization, and faster inference.

AI.tldr: HSD is a training-free framework for online video step grounding that uses a Large Multimodal Model to group streaming video into events and classify procedural steps. It reports substantial gains over state-of-the-art methods on HT-Step, Ego4D Goal-Step and CrossTask.
AI.motivation: Existing methods are either offline, requiring the full video, or online with fixed-length segments that yield noisy, over-segmented outputs. Coarse step descriptions also differ semantically from what is visually observed.
AI.method: Incoming segments are grouped incrementally into semantically consistent events, using an anchor caption validated against the visual stream. Zero-shot procedural step classification is applied to these events, and uncertain predictions are refined by decomposing candidate steps into finer substeps.
AI.result: HSD substantially outperforms state-of-the-art methods on HT-Step, Ego4D Goal-Step and CrossTask, with better step recognition, more accurate temporal localisation and faster inference. The abstract gives no specific figures.
AI.conclusion: Operating on semantically coherent events rather than fixed-length segments reduces redundant computation and gives more stable predictions.

title: EventSeeColor: Learning to Reconstruct Color from Monochrome Events
summary: Event cameras capture visual brightness changes under challenging lighting conditions. However, traditional event-based image reconstruction targets grayscale intensity and produces images without scene color. Color distinguishes surfaces with similar intensity. Reconstructing color from events can reveal appearance differences that reconstructed grayscale images cannot express. Although monochrome event cameras do not directly measure color, their event-triggering patterns depend on surface reflectance, illumination, and the sensor's spectral response. These patterns may contain cues that support color reconstruction. In this paper, we present EventSeeColor, which uses event-reconstructed grayscale and aligned events to jointly guide a diffusion colorizer. Grayscale-derived semantic context supports color inference, while region-balanced chroma supervision and local RGB refinement improve color distribution, brightness, and texture. In the combined evaluation on two real event datasets, EventSeeColor achieves the best structural similarity, learned perceptual scores, and chromatic-region color difference among the external methods.

AI.tldr: EventSeeColor reconstructs colour from monochrome event camera data by using event-reconstructed grayscale images and aligned events to guide a diffusion colorizer. It achieves the best structural similarity, learned perceptual scores and chromatic-region colour difference among external methods on two real event datasets.
AI.motivation: Traditional event-based reconstruction produces grayscale images without scene colour, although event triggering patterns depend on surface reflectance, illumination and the sensor's spectral response and may therefore carry colour cues.
AI.method: The model uses event-reconstructed grayscale images and aligned events jointly to guide a diffusion colorizer. Grayscale-derived semantic context supports colour inference, while region-balanced chroma supervision and local RGB refinement improve colour distribution, brightness and texture.
AI.result: On two real event datasets, the method achieves the best structural similarity, learned perceptual scores and chromatic-region colour difference among the external methods compared.
AI.conclusion: The results suggest that colour can be partly reconstructed from monochrome event data, revealing appearance differences that grayscale reconstructions cannot express.

title: Beyond CCT: Multi-channel SPD recovery for per-shot camera color correction
summary: Modern cameras correct color via two or three pre-calibrated 3x3 matrices interpolated by Correlated Color Temperature (CCT). This collapses the illuminant SPD to a scalar. LEDs, fluorescents, and mixed sources sit off the Planckian locus, and metameric illuminants with the same chromaticity demand different optimal CCMs that a CCT pipeline cannot distinguish. We recover the illuminant SPD instead using non-negative least squares against a basis dictionary, conditioned on the camera white point and a multi-channel ambient-light sensor (ALS). A closed-form 3x3 CCM is then fit per shot. On a synthetic benchmark of 300 illuminants and 3,100 reflectances, mean angular error drops from 1.89 to 1.20 degrees, with a 1.7x tail reduction on the LED-like off-Planckian group (n=45) where metameric ambiguity is tangible. The gain holds under realistic ALS imperfections and observation noise, and the same off-Planckian advantage carries over to 1,684 real measured SPDs.

AI.tldr: The paper recovers the illuminant spectral power distribution for each shot with non-negative least squares over a basis dictionary, then fits a 3x3 colour correction matrix. On a synthetic benchmark, mean angular error drops from 1.89 to 1.20 degrees.
AI.motivation: Camera colour correction interpolates pre-calibrated matrices by correlated colour temperature, which collapses the illuminant SPD to a scalar and cannot distinguish metameric illuminants or off-Planckian sources such as LEDs and fluorescents.
AI.method: The illuminant SPD is recovered with non-negative least squares against a basis dictionary, conditioned on the camera white point and a multi-channel ambient-light sensor. A closed-form 3x3 colour correction matrix is then fitted per shot.
AI.result: On a synthetic benchmark of 300 illuminants and 3,100 reflectances, mean angular error drops from 1.89 to 1.20 degrees, with a 1.7x tail reduction on the LED-like off-Planckian group (n=45). The gain holds under realistic sensor imperfections and noise, and carries over to 1,684 real measured SPDs.
AI.conclusion: Explicit SPD recovery improves per-shot colour correction, especially for off-Planckian illuminants where metameric ambiguity matters.

title: AdMuse: Skill-Guided Creative Advertising Image Generation
summary: An outstanding creative advertising image should both attract attention and communicate a product's positioning. How to choose a persuasive conceptual bridge before rendering begins is challenging for advertising generation. We present AdMuse, a skill-guided multi-agent framework that distills high-quality advertisements into reusable creative skills for cross-domain advertising strategy. Rather than retrieving isolated exemplars, AdMuse abstracts recurring bridge patterns into a skill library that can guide new product briefs. At generation time, AdMuse coordinates skill routing, multi-candidate ideation and selection, and VLM-guided visual refinement: diverse skills propose alternative concepts, relative judgment selects the most promising direction, and vision-language feedback helps realize the selected intent in the final image. This design treats advertising creativity as a structured decision process rather than a single prompt-writing step. Experiments across diverse product and brand positionings show that AdMuse produces visually compelling advertisements that faithfully communicate product positioning.

AI.tldr: AdMuse is a skill-guided multi-agent framework that generates creative advertising images by distilling recurring bridge patterns into a reusable skill library. It selects a conceptual bridge before rendering and then refines the image with vision-language feedback.
AI.motivation: Choosing a persuasive conceptual bridge before rendering is difficult in advertising generation, and retrieving isolated exemplars does not capture the recurring strategy behind high-quality advertisements.
AI.method: Recurring bridge patterns are abstracted into a skill library that guides new product briefs. At generation time, skill routing, multi-candidate ideation with relative selection, and VLM-guided visual refinement are coordinated.
AI.result: Experiments across diverse product and brand positionings show visually compelling advertisements that faithfully communicate product positioning. The abstract gives no quantitative results or baselines.
AI.conclusion: Treating advertising creativity as a structured decision process rather than a single prompt-writing step is presented as the key design choice.

title: Video Generation Meets Agent Harness: Agentic Video Generation, Agentic World Modeling and Recursive Self-Improvement
comment: website: this https URL github: this https URL
summary: Video generation is shifting from end-to-end synthesis toward agentic generation, where planning, tool use, and feedback enable coherent, controllable multi-shot videos. In parallel, video world models provide action-conditioned observations and predicted futures, serving as interactive environments for agents. We study their intersection through the agent harness: an executable runtime that constructs context, exposes tools, maintains state, routes feedback, and manages budgets around video models. This report examines three directions. First, agentic video generation, where harnesses coordinate scripting, shot planning, asset management, production, and editing, alongside the evaluation challenges of these systems. Second, agentic world modeling, where harnesses mediate observation, control, execution, and state. We discuss hybrid designs in which game engines or agent-written programs maintain world state while video models render observations, and how agents and world models can mutually evaluate and improve one another. Third, recursive self-improvement (RSI) in video model development, distinguishing output revisions, updates to harness state, generator parameters, and evaluators, and changes to the improvement procedure itself. We identify how these improvements feed back into subsequent development. Across these directions, we analyze essential agent capabilities, including audiovisual perception, long-horizon planning, memory, code-based interaction, feedback-guided control, skill reuse, and multi-agent coordination. We conclude with challenges in autonomous video production, lifelong memory, programmable hybrid control, autonomous model development, provenance, cost accounting, and evaluation linking video quality and task performance to sustained improvements in models and harnesses.

AI.tldr: This report examines the intersection of agentic video generation, video world models and recursive self-improvement through the notion of an agent harness, an executable runtime around video models. It surveys three directions and the agent capabilities and challenges they raise.
AI.motivation: Video generation is shifting from end-to-end synthesis toward agentic generation, and video world models serve as interactive environments for agents. The authors frame the intersection through the agent harness, which constructs context, exposes tools, maintains state, routes feedback and manages budgets.
AI.method: The report is a discussion rather than an experimental study. It covers agentic video generation with coordinated scripting, planning, production and editing; agentic world modelling with hybrid designs in which game engines or agent-written programs maintain state while video models render observations; and recursive self-improvement distinguishing output revisions, harness state, generator parameters, evaluators and the improvement procedure itself.
AI.result: The abstract reports no experimental results. It analyses essential agent capabilities, including audiovisual perception, long-horizon planning, memory, code-based interaction, feedback-guided control, skill reuse and multi-agent coordination.
AI.conclusion: The report closes with open challenges in autonomous video production, lifelong memory, programmable hybrid control, autonomous model development, provenance, cost accounting and evaluation linking video quality to sustained improvement.

title: Benchmarking color judgment in multimodal LLMs with CIE-computable ground truth
summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are now used as zero-shot judges of image quality, but their color judgments are rarely tested with colorimetric ground truth. We present a five-task benchmark based on the CIE colorimetric framework: AWB pair judgment, skin-tone bias direction, CCT estimation, CIE Delta E 2000 pair ordering, and color naming under changing illuminants. We test eight MLLM endpoints, including four Qwen3-VL variants, GLM-4.5V, GPT-5.4, Claude-Opus-4.7, and Gemini-3.1-Pro. The models often solve coarse binary AWB judgments, but they remain weak on numeric CCT estimation and on some fine color-difference judgments. On ColorChecker-24 stimuli, the three closed-weight frontier models reach CCT MAE of 715-1056 K, compared with 1358-2133 K for the five open-weight models. A non-ColorChecker control shows that this advantage is partly template-dependent. The results suggest that current MLLMs have useful color words and coarse visual priors, but their color judgments are not reliably calibrated to CIE-computable color differences.

AI.tldr: A five-task benchmark based on CIE colorimetry tests eight MLLM endpoints on colour judgment. Coarse binary white-balance judgments are often solved, but numeric colour temperature estimation and fine colour differences remain weak, and closed-weight frontier models give lower CCT error than open-weight models on ColorChecker-24 stimuli.
AI.motivation: MLLMs are increasingly used as zero-shot judges of image quality, yet their colour judgments are rarely tested against colorimetric ground truth.
AI.method: The benchmark has five tasks: AWB pair judgment, skin-tone bias direction, CCT estimation, CIE Delta E 2000 pair ordering, and colour naming under changing illuminants. Eight endpoints are tested, including four Qwen3-VL variants, GLM-4.5V, GPT-5.4, Claude-Opus-4.7 and Gemini-3.1-Pro.
AI.result: On ColorChecker-24 stimuli, the three closed-weight frontier models reach CCT MAE of 715-1056 K, against 1358-2133 K for the five open-weight models. A non-ColorChecker control shows the advantage is partly template-dependent.
AI.conclusion: Current MLLMs have useful colour vocabulary and coarse visual priors, but their colour judgments are not reliably calibrated to CIE-computable colour differences.

title: TaskFrame: Connecting Task-Level Planning with Frame-Level Control for Game Agents
summary: Building general game agents requires both high-level task reasoning and low-latency action control in rapidly changing visual environments. These capabilities favor models with substantially different computational profiles, making them difficult to realize within a single model. In this work, we present TaskFrame, a hierarchical planner-controller framework that connects task-level planning with frame-level keyboard-and-mouse control. A vision-language task planner decomposes a high-level goal into an ordered sequence of atomic instructions and is optimized through supervised learning and dependency-aware GRPO. The hidden states of special goal tokens that terminate each atomic instruction provide continuous goal embeddings that are cached and reused across control steps. A causal Transformer controller combines the embedding of the active goal with recent observations to predict discrete keyboard and mouse-button actions and continuous camera motion at every game step. We train the system in three stages: planner training, controller pretraining, and joint alignment. Experiments in Minecraft show that TaskFrame is competitive with general-purpose vision-language models on instruction decomposition, and that in closed-loop evaluation the agent achieves a higher combat success rate than the evaluated baselines.

AI.tldr: TaskFrame is a hierarchical planner-controller for Minecraft game agents that connects a vision-language task planner with a frame-level causal Transformer controller for keyboard, mouse and camera actions. In closed-loop evaluation it achieves a higher combat success rate than the evaluated baselines.
AI.motivation: General game agents need both high-level task reasoning and low-latency control, which favour models with very different computational profiles and are hard to combine in a single model.
AI.method: A vision-language planner decomposes goals into ordered atomic instructions, trained with supervised learning and dependency-aware GRPO. Hidden states of goal tokens are cached as continuous goal embeddings. A causal Transformer controller combines the active goal embedding with recent observations to predict discrete keyboard and mouse-button actions and continuous camera motion at every step. Training has three stages: planner training, controller pretraining and joint alignment.
AI.result: The planner is competitive with general-purpose vision-language models on instruction decomposition, and in closed-loop Minecraft evaluation the agent achieves a higher combat success rate than the evaluated baselines.
AI.conclusion: Separating task-level planning from frame-level control, linked by reusable goal embeddings, is presented as a workable design for game agents.

title: LoRe-MIM: Lost-or-Replaced Masked Image Modeling for Self-Supervised Representation Learning in Whole-Body PET/CT
summary: Deep learning models for whole-body positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) hold significant clinical potential for disease detection, treatment planning, and response assessment. However, the time and cost associated with expert annotations remain major bottlenecks in developing robust and generalizable models. Although self-supervised learning (SSL) has emerged as a promising approach to mitigating annotation scarcity, its application to whole-body PET/CT remains relatively underexplored due to the limited availability of large-scale datasets and the challenges associated with learning complementary cross-modal representations. To address these limitations, we curate a heterogeneous, multi-tracer, multi-institutional cohort comprising 6,531 whole-body PET/CT scans and propose LoRe-MIM (Lost-Or-Replaced Masked Image Modelling), a novel self-supervised framework designed to learn multimodal representations through masked image reconstruction. Specifically, LoRe-MIM introduces a masking strategy in which image regions are either replaced with zeros (Lost) or substituted with corresponding complementary imaging modality (Replaced), encouraging the model to capture both modality-specific characteristics and cross-modal relationships. We evaluate the learned representations across multiple downstream tasks, including multimodal PET/CT image reconstruction, patch-based classification into cancer vs. non-cancer, whole-body lesion segmentation, label-efficient training, and robustness assessment. Experimental results demonstrate that LoRe-MIM consistently outperforms the corresponding state-of-the-art baselines across these tasks, highlighting its potential as a scalable and generalizable self-supervised learning framework for whole-body PET/CT analysis.

AI.tldr: LoRe-MIM is a self-supervised masked image modelling framework for whole-body PET/CT that replaces image regions either with zeros (Lost) or with the complementary modality (Replaced). It is pre-trained on a curated cohort of 6,531 scans and outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across the evaluated downstream tasks.
AI.motivation: Annotation scarcity limits deep learning for whole-body PET/CT, and self-supervised learning remains underexplored there because large-scale datasets are scarce and cross-modal representations are hard to learn.
AI.method: A heterogeneous multi-tracer, multi-institutional cohort of 6,531 whole-body PET/CT scans is curated. The masking strategy replaces image regions with zeros (Lost) or substitutes the corresponding complementary imaging modality (Replaced), encouraging both modality-specific and cross-modal representations.
AI.result: The learned representations are evaluated on multimodal PET/CT reconstruction, patch-based cancer vs non-cancer classification, whole-body lesion segmentation, label-efficient training and robustness, where LoRe-MIM consistently outperforms the corresponding state-of-the-art baselines. The abstract gives no numbers.
AI.conclusion: LoRe-MIM is presented as a scalable and generalisable self-supervised framework for whole-body PET/CT analysis.

title: Self-training for cross-centre coronary vessel segmentation in X-ray angiography using pre-contrast frame subtraction
summary: Deep learning models for coronary vessel segmentation in X-ray angiography often perform poorly on data from centres that were not represented in training. Apart from differences in equipment, the labels of the largest public dataset (ARCADE) are incomplete, as only the segments defined in the SYNTAX score are annotated. In this study, we evaluated whether self-training with pseudo-labels can improve performance on external data without additional manual annotation. Pseudo-labels were generated from two sources, namely the predictions of an nnU-Net model trained on ARCADE and a contrast map obtained by subtracting a pre-contrast frame from the same sequence. The nnU-Net predictions were extended along the contrast map, and pixels detected only in the subtraction image were assigned an ignore label and excluded from the loss. Six models were trained and tested on ARCADE and on two external datasets (XCAD and XACV). All first-round models initialised with the baseline predictions performed better than both the baseline and a control model fine-tuned for the same number of epochs. The model trained on the XCAD pool improved the macro-averaged Dice score by 2.7 points (95% CI 2.3-3.2), while the control decreased it by 0.6 points. A second round of self-training did not lead to further improvement. When an external model trained on 50 fully annotated images was used to generate the initial labels, the XCAD Dice score increased from 0.623 to 0.745 without any XCAD labels, although performance on XACV did not improve because large main vessels were missed. These results suggest that the benefit of self-training depends largely on the sensitivity of the model used to generate the initial pseudo-labels.

AI.tldr: Self-training with pseudo-labels from an nnU-Net and a pre-contrast frame subtraction map improves coronary vessel segmentation in X-ray angiography on external datasets without new manual annotation. On XCAD, Dice rises from 0.623 to 0.745 when the initial labels come from a model trained on 50 annotated images.
AI.motivation: Coronary segmentation models generalise poorly to centres not represented in training, and the largest public dataset, ARCADE, is incompletely labelled because only SYNTAX-defined segments are annotated.
AI.method: Pseudo-labels combine nnU-Net predictions trained on ARCADE, extended along a contrast map obtained by subtracting a pre-contrast frame from the same sequence. Pixels detected only in the subtraction image receive an ignore label and are excluded from the loss. Six models are trained and tested on ARCADE and on the external XCAD and XACV datasets.
AI.result: The model trained on the XCAD pool improves macro-averaged Dice by 2.7 points (95% CI 2.3-3.2), while the control decreases it by 0.6 points. A second round gives no further gain. With an external model trained on 50 fully annotated images for the initial labels, XCAD Dice rises from 0.623 to 0.745, but XACV does not improve because large main vessels are missed.
AI.conclusion: The benefit of self-training depends largely on the sensitivity of the model that generates the initial pseudo-labels.

title: Textual Response-Aware Guidance for Zero-Shot Adversarial Robustness of Vision-Language Models
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit strong zero-shot generalization but remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks. Existing adversarial fine-tuning methods often use pre-trained model guidance to preserve image--text alignment while improving robustness. Our analysis of visual representation drift reveals complementary limitations of two representative forms of guidance. Matching visual features provides broad coverage by constraining all directions equally, but lacks semantic emphasis. Matching prediction distributions prioritizes semantically relevant directions, but remains limited by the candidate texts and prediction probabilities. These limitations can hinder preservation of pre-trained image--text relationships and degrade zero-shot performance. To address these issues, we propose Textual Response-Aware Guidance (TRAG), which constrains visual representation drift using the pre-trained text encoder's responses to local variations in input embeddings. Specifically, TRAG constructs anchor-level constraints from the response directions and magnitudes around semantic anchors, then aggregates them using pre-trained image--anchor relevance, yielding an image-adaptive constraint. Extensive experiments across architectures and tasks demonstrate state-of-the-art clean and robust performance. Further analysis shows that TRAG helps preserve pre-trained image--text relationships.

AI.tldr: TRAG is a guidance method for adversarial fine-tuning of vision-language models that constrains visual representation drift using the pre-trained text encoder's responses to local input perturbations. It reports state-of-the-art clean and robust performance across architectures and tasks.
AI.motivation: Matching visual features constrains all directions equally without semantic emphasis, and matching prediction distributions is limited by the candidate texts and probabilities, so both can hinder preservation of pre-trained image-text relationships and degrade zero-shot performance.
AI.method: Anchor-level constraints are built from the response directions and magnitudes around semantic anchors, then aggregated using pre-trained image-anchor relevance to yield an image-adaptive constraint.
AI.result: The abstract reports state-of-the-art clean and robust performance in extensive experiments across architectures and tasks, and further analysis shows that TRAG helps preserve pre-trained image-text relationships. No specific numbers are given.
AI.conclusion: Constraining representation drift with text-encoder responses helps preserve pre-trained image-text relationships during adversarial robustness training.

title: Radiology Guideline-derived Decision Graph for Efficient Clinical Decision Support
summary: Radiological risk stratification and management planning are essential downstream tasks in medical imaging. Automating these tasks is challenging because clinical guideline criteria are distributed across prose, tables, and cross-referenced definitions. We present Guideline-derived Decision Graph (GDGraph), a framework that decouples guideline compilation from case evaluation. During compilation, a large language model partitions guidelines into section-based chunks, extracts local decision subgraphs with linked definitions, and aggregates related branches into an executable decision graph. During inference, a fast System One model answers localized clinical questions while deterministic traversal resolves Boolean logic, turning opaque single-pass predictions into a traceable decision path without task-specific training. Across 347 cases spanning renal cyst, adnexal mass, and thyroid nodule guidelines, GDGraph improves System One accuracy from 57.3% to 90.8%, outperforming retrieval-augmented GPT-4o (80.1%) and graph-guided GPT-4o with chain-of-thought (82.7%) at substantially lower latency and cost. The source code will be available.

AI.tldr: GDGraph compiles clinical guidelines into an executable decision graph with an LLM, then answers case questions with a fast model plus deterministic traversal, raising System One accuracy on 347 radiology cases from 57.3% to 90.8% without task-specific training.
AI.motivation: Radiological risk stratification depends on guideline criteria spread across prose, tables and cross-referenced definitions, which makes automating these decisions hard.
AI.method: A framework that decouples guideline compilation from case evaluation: an LLM partitions guidelines into section-based chunks, extracts local decision subgraphs with linked definitions and aggregates them into one decision graph; at inference a fast System One model answers localized questions while deterministic traversal resolves the Boolean logic, yielding a traceable decision path.
AI.result: Across 347 cases spanning renal cyst, adnexal mass and thyroid nodule guidelines, System One accuracy rose from 57.3% to 90.8%, above retrieval-augmented GPT-4o (80.1%) and graph-guided GPT-4o with chain-of-thought (82.7%), at substantially lower latency and cost.
AI.conclusion: Compiling guidelines into an executable graph turns opaque single-pass predictions into traceable decision paths, offering a more accurate and cheaper route to clinical decision support without task-specific training.

title: RFW-A: Agentic Procedural Generation of 400K Articulated Assets over 500 Categories
comment: 37 pages, 19 figures. Project Page: this https URL
summary: High-quality articulated assets are essential for embodied perception, simulation, and manipulation, yet constructing them at scale remains difficult. Manual annotation and procedural modeling require substantial human effort. Recent agentic systems automate asset construction through program synthesis, but repeat costly reasoning and refinement for every new asset. Our key observation is that assets within a category can share construction logic despite variations in structure and appearance. Agentic synthesis and procedural generation are therefore complementary: agents can construct reusable programs, while procedural execution reuses the resulting logic across many samples. We therefore present RFW-A, which combines the two in a new articulated-asset generation paradigm. Starting from existing articulated programs, RFW-A organizes reusable components and their dependencies into category-level generators. Agents test and refine these generators across sampled configurations and motion states. Once constructed and validated, the generators produce diverse assets through procedural execution with no further model calls or token charges. The estimated API cost of generator authoring averages $10.62, amortizing to $0.05 per asset over 200 assets, versus $1.24 for the sampled per-asset agentic synthesis baseline. Using RFW-A, we built RFW-A-400K, containing over 400K sim-ready articulated assets across more than 500 categories. Experiments show high structural and kinematic validity and stable execution across physics simulators. Beyond asset validity, training with RFW-A-400K improves part-level articulation estimation on seen and unseen categories, while policies trained in simulation with retrieved and program-edited assets transfer zero-shot to real articulated objects.

AI.tldr: RFW-A uses agents to write reusable category-level generator programs, then procedurally executes them to produce over 400K simulation-ready articulated assets across more than 500 categories without further model calls.
AI.motivation: Manual annotation and procedural modeling need heavy human effort, while agentic program synthesis repeats costly reasoning and refinement for every new asset.
AI.method: Starting from existing articulated programs, reusable components and their dependencies are organized into category-level generators; agents test and refine these generators across sampled configurations and motion states, and validated generators then produce assets through procedural execution.
AI.result: Generator authoring costs an estimated $10.62 on average, amortizing to $0.05 per asset over 200 assets, versus $1.24 per asset for the per-asset agentic synthesis baseline. The RFW-A-400K dataset shows high structural and kinematic validity and stable execution across physics simulators; training on it improves part-level articulation estimation on seen and unseen categories, and simulation policies trained with retrieved and program-edited assets transfer zero-shot to real articulated objects.
AI.conclusion: Sharing construction logic within a category and amortizing agent cost over many procedurally executed samples makes large-scale, sim-ready articulated asset construction practical.

title: Wizard: Manipulate Any World in Real Time via Agentic Control
summary: Recent advances in video world models have enabled the generation of increasingly realistic and interactive virtual environments, opening new possibilities for player-customizable gameplay. Agentic frameworks further advance this direction by decoupling explicit game logic and controllable world representations from visual generation. However, existing approaches support only simple game settings and predefined motion patterns, generalize poorly to unseen environments and characters, and offer limited real-time interactivity. In this paper, we introduce Wizard, an agentic game world model that enables real-time, precise control over character motions while generalizing zero-shot across novel scenes, characters, and actions. To achieve this, we construct a diverse dataset spanning 750 scenes and 178 characters, incorporating skeleton and geometry information as structured representations. We leverage these representations as intermediate proxies to condition a video generation model, together with an adaptive masking mechanism that improves alignment between the conditioning signals and generated video rollouts. Furthermore, we introduce an agentic framework that explicitly maintains and updates game states, allowing players to freely configure their virtual worlds and exercise fine-grained control over character motions while preserving visual quality and gameplay consistency. By combining agentic control with structured proxy-based generation, our framework unlocks new possibilities for player-driven game creation with real-time, generalizable, and mechanically consistent world simulation.

AI.tldr: Wizard is an agentic game world model that gives real-time, precise control over character motion and generalizes zero-shot to novel scenes, characters and actions.
AI.motivation: Existing approaches support only simple game settings and predefined motion patterns, generalize poorly to unseen environments and characters, and offer limited real-time interactivity.
AI.method: A dataset of 750 scenes and 178 characters with skeleton and geometry information serves as structured intermediate proxies that condition a video generation model, with an adaptive masking mechanism to improve alignment; an agentic framework explicitly maintains and updates game states so players can configure worlds and control character motion.
AI.result: The abstract reports no quantitative results; it claims real-time, generalizable and mechanically consistent world simulation while preserving visual quality and gameplay consistency.
AI.conclusion: Combining agentic state control with proxy-based generation is presented as enabling player-driven game creation with real-time, generalizable world simulation.

title: HiFOR: Hierarchical Foresight with Action-Guided World Grounding for Vision-Language-Action Model
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated promising capabilities in robotic manipulation by integrating visual perception, language understanding, and action generation. Recent advances have further incorporated future prediction to enhance the understanding of environmental dynamics and task progression. However, existing methods often model short-term dynamics and long-term task objectives separately, while directly incorporating predicted futures into action policies without sufficiently considering their relevance to current action requirements. To address these limitations, we propose HiFOR, a hierarchical foresight framework with action-guided world retrieval. Specifically, Hierarchical Foresight Prediction jointly predicts short-term state evolution, semantic milestones, and final goal states through a Hierarchical Dependency Mask (HDM), establishing dependencies across temporal horizons. Building upon these predictions, Structure-Aware Latent World Modeling organizes future latent representations along the horizon, view, and spatial dimensions to facilitate fine-grained retrieval. Furthermore, Action-Guided Factorized World Retrieval adaptively retrieves relevant future information from the structured latent world based on evolving action representations during denoising, providing targeted guidance for action generation. Extensive experiments on two simulation benchmarks and six real-world robotic manipulation tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

AI.tldr: HiFOR is a hierarchical foresight framework for vision-language-action robot policies that predicts future states at several time horizons and retrieves relevant future information guided by the current action representation.
AI.motivation: Existing methods model short-term dynamics and long-term task objectives separately and feed predicted futures into action policies without considering how relevant they are to current action requirements.
AI.method: Hierarchical Foresight Prediction jointly predicts short-term state evolution, semantic milestones and final goal states through a Hierarchical Dependency Mask; Structure-Aware Latent World Modeling organizes future latents along horizon, view and spatial dimensions; Action-Guided Factorized World Retrieval retrieves relevant future information during denoising based on evolving action representations.
AI.result: The abstract reports that experiments on two simulation benchmarks and six real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate effectiveness, without specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Action-guided retrieval from a structured, hierarchical latent world is presented as an effective way to give policies targeted future guidance for action generation.

title: PhysInsert: Physically Plausible Object Insertion with Geometric Priors and Bidirectional Object-Scene Interactions
comment: 51 pages, including supplementary material. Project page: this https URL
summary: We present PhysInsert, a framework for physically plausible reference-based object insertion that jointly adapts objects and their surrounding scenes. Existing methods often rely on masked inputs, generation-based pairs, or training pairs with limited viewpoint variation, leaving pose and illumination adaptation and bidirectional object-scene interactions insufficiently constrained. We construct the Insert World dataset with strictly aligned Blender-rendered counterfactual pairs and object references across viewpoints and lighting conditions. Building on these data, Geometry-Guided Adaptation couples a VGGT geometry stream with image and text streams under target-scene feature supervision to guide spatially consistent insertion. Complementary 2D Object-Scene Spatial Supervision jointly supervises object occupancy and environmental changes while grounding spatial instructions in object regions through image-text attention. We introduce PhysInsert-Bench with dedicated cross-environment and cross-view cases requiring illumination and pose adaptation beyond appearance copying. Experiments on PhysInsert-Bench and DreamBooth demonstrate improved image fidelity; a user study further shows more accurate placement and improved lighting integration, perspective, and pose plausibility.

AI.tldr: PhysInsert inserts a reference object into a scene with physically plausible pose, illumination and perspective by jointly adapting the object and its surroundings.
AI.motivation: Existing object insertion methods rely on masked inputs, generation-based pairs or training pairs with limited viewpoint variation, leaving pose and illumination adaptation and bidirectional object-scene interactions insufficiently constrained.
AI.method: The Insert World dataset provides strictly aligned Blender-rendered counterfactual pairs across viewpoints and lighting; Geometry-Guided Adaptation couples a VGGT geometry stream with image and text streams under target-scene feature supervision; 2D Object-Scene Spatial Supervision supervises object occupancy and environmental changes and grounds spatial instructions in object regions through image-text attention.
AI.result: Experiments on the newly introduced PhysInsert-Bench and on DreamBooth show improved image fidelity; a user study reports more accurate placement and better lighting integration, perspective and pose plausibility.
AI.conclusion: Jointly adapting objects and scenes with geometric priors and bidirectional supervision moves insertion beyond appearance copying toward physically plausible placement.

title: A Unified Benchmark for Aerial-Enhanced Autonomous Driving: The KITScenes Aerial Dataset
comment: Accepted at the IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV 2027)
summary: Aerial imagery provides complementary spatial context for autonomous driving by exposing road structure beyond the immediate perception range of onboard sensors. Yet map construction from aerial imagery, aerial-assisted online HD mapping, and cross-view localization are typically studied on separate data and benchmarks. We introduce KITScenes Aerial, an extension of the KITScenes Multimodal dataset that augments synchronized onboard sensor data, vehicle poses, and rich Lanelet2 map annotations with spatially associated aerial imagery and higher-resolution neural representations, providing a common basis for a variety of research tasks. Our mapping evaluation focuses on all 53 KITScenes map classes across different model designs, spatial ranges, and aerial resolutions, while retaining compatibility with the widely used three-class setting. Representative baselines show that aerial context is particularly beneficial for fine-grained and extended-range mapping, more than doubling 53-class mAP at the larger mapping extent. Higher-resolution aerial imagery yields a further 4.3 mAP (+24 %) improvement, with gains extending to challenging map elements such as traffic lights. We additionally evaluate cross-view localization under geographically disjoint conditions, where an adapted fine-grained feature-matching baseline achieves a mean translation error of 5.13 m. KITScenes Aerial thus enables unified study of aerial and ground-level information across complementary mapping and localization tasks. Project page: this https URL

AI.tldr: KITScenes Aerial extends the KITScenes multimodal dataset with aerial imagery and neural representations, providing a common benchmark for aerial-assisted mapping and cross-view localization in autonomous driving.
AI.motivation: Map construction from aerial imagery, aerial-assisted online HD mapping and cross-view localization are usually studied on separate data and benchmarks.
AI.method: The dataset adds spatially associated aerial imagery and higher-resolution neural representations to synchronized onboard sensor data, vehicle poses and Lanelet2 map annotations; mapping is evaluated on all 53 KITScenes map classes across model designs, spatial ranges and aerial resolutions, and cross-view localization under geographically disjoint conditions.
AI.result: Aerial context mainly helps fine-grained, extended-range mapping, more than doubling 53-class mAP at the larger mapping extent; higher-resolution aerial imagery adds a further 4.3 mAP (+24%), with gains on challenging elements such as traffic lights; an adapted fine-grained feature-matching baseline reaches a mean translation error of 5.13 m in cross-view localization.
AI.conclusion: The benchmark enables unified study of aerial and ground-level information across complementary mapping and localization tasks.

title: InfantNet: A Large Scale Dataset for Infant Body Pose and Shape Estimation
summary: Infant pose and shape estimation is essential for applications in childcare, developmental monitoring, and medical diagnosis. However, existing methods and datasets are largely designed for adults, and direct transfer to infants fails due to substantial differences in body proportions, articulation limits, and frequent self-occlusion. To address this gap, we introduce InfantNet, the largest real-image infant dataset to date, comprising 108,902 RGB images of infants aged 6-18 months. Each image is annotated with 2D keypoints, and a curated subset of 11,642 images additionally includes 3D pose and shape annotations with full SMIL parameters, verified through multi-view rendering and reprojection-error filtering. We use an iterative annotation pipeline to ensure high fidelity across both 2D and 3D labels. InfantNet establishes a large-scale, comprehensive benchmark for infant 2D keypoint detection and 3D pose-and-shape recovery. Baseline experiments demonstrate that state-of-the-art adult pose estimators do not generalize well to infants, whereas fine-tuning on InfantNet yields a consistent improvement. The gains are even more pronounced for 3D pose and shape estimation, where SMIL-based estimation demonstrates robust performance with accuracy comparable to results reported for SMPL-based models. By releasing the InfantNet dataset and benchmark, we provide a vital resource for advancing infant pose analysis and related healthcare applications.

AI.tldr: InfantNet is a large real-image infant dataset of 108,902 RGB images with 2D keypoints and, for 11,642 of them, 3D pose and shape annotations with full SMIL parameters.
AI.motivation: Pose and shape estimation methods and datasets are designed for adults, and direct transfer to infants fails because of differences in body proportions, articulation limits and frequent self-occlusion.
AI.method: An iterative annotation pipeline labels 2D keypoints for all images and, for a curated subset, 3D pose and shape with full SMIL parameters, verified through multi-view rendering and reprojection-error filtering.
AI.result: State-of-the-art adult pose estimators do not generalize well to infants, while fine-tuning on InfantNet gives consistent improvements, most pronounced for 3D pose and shape; SMIL-based estimation reaches accuracy comparable to reported SMPL-based results.
AI.conclusion: The dataset and benchmark provide a resource for advancing infant pose analysis and related healthcare applications.

title: Accurate MRI-free PET Quantification and Reliability Assessment via CT-to-MRI Synthesis and Conformal Prediction
comment: 28 pages, 8 figures, including supplementary material. Submitted to Medical Image Analysis
summary: Standardized uptake value ratio (SUVR) quantification of amyloid PET commonly relies on a subject-specific T1-weighted MRI, yet a usable MRI is not always available. We therefore combined CT-to-MRI synthesis with conformal prediction for MRI-free PET quantification with reliability assessment. A slice-consistent Brownian Bridge Diffusion Model was strengthened with multi-dataset training and data-source conditioning to enrich the anatomical prior learned from MRI, and with expanded multi-slice CT context to exploit the through-plane continuity of subject-specific anatomy in CT. Synthetic MRI was used for FreeSurfer-based anatomical parcellation and PET quantification, while deep-ensemble uncertainty was calibrated with conformal prediction to estimate a plausible range for the corresponding real MRI-based SUVR. On $^{11}$C-PiB PET from OASIS-3, the proposed method achieved the highest synthesis and parcellation fidelity among the compared methods. Mean cortical SUVR from the proposed synthetic MRI agreed closely with the real MRI-based reference (MAE $0.016 \pm 0.015$, Pearson $r = 0.9987$) and yielded the same amyloid-positivity classification as the real MRI in all 87 test subjects at the prespecified cut-off. Conformal prediction achieved empirical coverage close to the prespecified levels, and at 90% target coverage, 85 of 87 subjects had prediction intervals that supported an unambiguous amyloid-positivity decision. Zero-shot evaluation on an independent external cohort showed that the proposed CT-to-MRI model could support PET quantification without retraining, although conformal calibration required target-cohort recalibration to recover the intended coverage. These findings support CT-to-MRI-based MRI-free PET quantification as a promising approach for providing accurate SUVR measurements and an explicit assessment of their reliability.

AI.tldr: A CT-to-MRI synthesis model combined with conformal prediction enables MRI-free amyloid PET SUVR quantification and gives a calibrated plausible range alongside the value.
AI.motivation: SUVR quantification of amyloid PET normally relies on a subject-specific T1-weighted MRI, which is not always available.
AI.method: A slice-consistent Brownian Bridge Diffusion Model, strengthened with multi-dataset training, data-source conditioning and multi-slice CT context, synthesizes MRI for FreeSurfer-based parcellation; deep-ensemble uncertainty is calibrated with conformal prediction to estimate a range for the real MRI-based SUVR.
AI.result: On 11C-PiB PET from OASIS-3, synthetic-MRI cortical SUVR agreed closely with the real-MRI reference (MAE 0.016 +/- 0.015, Pearson r = 0.9987) and gave the same amyloid-positivity classification in all 87 test subjects; at 90% target coverage, 85 of 87 subjects had intervals that supported an unambiguous decision. Zero-shot evaluation on an external cohort worked, but conformal calibration needed target-cohort recalibration to recover the intended coverage.
AI.conclusion: CT-to-MRI synthesis with conformal reliability assessment is a promising route to accurate MRI-free SUVR measurements with an explicit assessment of their uncertainty.

title: AVPS-360: A Spatial Audio-Visual Benchmark for Instance Segmentation and Tracking of Sound-Producing Persons
summary: Audio-visual instance segmentation (AVIS) segments and tracks individual sound-producing objects in videos. Existing benchmarks predominantly use monaural audio, which lacks inter-channel cues for spatially distinguishing concurrent sound sources. We introduce AVPS-360 (Audio-Visual Person Segmentation 360), a spatial audio-visual benchmark bridging AVIS and sound event localisation and detection (SELD). Built upon STARSS23, it pairs first-order Ambisonics audio with synchronised 360° video across 230 recordings totalling 10.5 hours. Recordings average 164.0 seconds. The dataset captures intermittent sound production in real-world interactions dominated by speech, alongside laughter, clapping, and footsteps. It provides 31,678 manually reviewed instance masks linked to source identities and sound-event labels. We also present a baseline that integrates spatial audio with visual features for frame-level segmentation and identity association across frames. Experiments on AVPS-360 show that existing AVIS methods struggle with detection and identity association in long recordings with intermittent sound production, while our baseline substantially improves performance in both aspects.

AI.tldr: AVPS-360 is a spatial audio-visual benchmark pairing first-order Ambisonics audio with 360-degree video for instance segmentation and tracking of sound-producing persons.
AI.motivation: Existing audio-visual instance segmentation benchmarks use monaural audio, which lacks the inter-channel cues needed to spatially separate concurrent sound sources.
AI.method: Built on STARSS23, the benchmark covers 230 recordings totalling 10.5 hours (averaging 164.0 seconds) and provides 31,678 manually reviewed instance masks linked to source identities and sound-event labels; the baseline integrates spatial audio with visual features for frame-level segmentation and identity association across frames.
AI.result: Existing audio-visual instance segmentation methods struggle with detection and identity association in long recordings with intermittent sound production, while the baseline substantially improves both.
AI.conclusion: The benchmark bridges audio-visual instance segmentation and sound event localization and detection, exposing the limits of current methods in realistic spatial audio-visual settings.

title: MetaRefine: Score Refinement with Multi-Level Features for Image Assessment
